title.zh: 卷九十九 列傳第五十九 二凶
title.raw: 卷九十九 列傳第五十九 二凶 Volume 99 Biographies 59: Er Xiong

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十九 二凶

translations.literal: Biographies 59: The Two Villains
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 59: The Two Villains

sentences.zh: 元兇劭，字休遠，文帝長子也。

translations.literal: The Primary Villain Liu Shao, style name Xiuyuan, was Emperor Wen's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shao—the posthumous title "Primary Villain" would later condemn him—styled himself Xiuyuan and was the eldest son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 帝即位後生劭，時上猶在諒闇，故秘之。

translations.literal: Shao was born after the emperor had taken the throne; the emperor was still in mourning seclusion, so it was kept secret.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was born after Wen had already ascended the throne, while the emperor was still observing mourning seclusion, so the birth was concealed.

sentences.zh: 三年閏正月，方云劭生。

translations.literal: In the intercalary first month of the third year, it was only then announced that Shao had been born.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the intercalary first month of the third year was Shao's birth publicly announced.

sentences.zh: 自前代以來，未有人君即位後皇后生太子，唯殷帝乙既踐阼，正妃生紂，至是又有劭焉。

translations.literal: From former ages onward, there had never been a case of an empress giving birth to the heir apparent after her lord had already taken the throne—only after King Yi of Yin had ascended the steps, his principal consort bore Zhou; now there was Shao as well.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout earlier history no ruler's empress had borne a crown prince after her husband was already on the throne; the sole precedent was King Yi of the Yin, whose principal consort bore Zhou after his accession—and now Shao offered another such case.

sentences.zh: 體元居正，上甚喜說。

translations.literal: He embodied the primal origin and occupied the correct position; the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: As the legitimate heir who embodied the dynasty's primal legitimacy, he delighted the emperor exceedingly.

sentences.zh: 年六歲，拜為皇太子，中庶子二率入直永福省。

translations.literal: At age six he was appointed crown prince; two leaders of the palace attendants entered duty at the Yongfu Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At six he was invested as crown prince, and two chiefs of the palace attendants took up residence in the Yongfu Bureau on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 更築宮，制度嚴麗。

translations.literal: They rebuilt his palace; its regulations were strict and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: A new palace was constructed for him, imposing in scale and sumptuous in appointment.

sentences.zh: 年十二，出居東宮，納黃門侍郎殷淳女為妃。

translations.literal: At twelve he moved out to reside in the Eastern Palace and took as consort the daughter of Yellow Gate Attendant-Cadet Yin Chun.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he left the inner quarters for the Eastern Palace and married the daughter of Yin Chun, Attendant-Cadet of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 十三，加元服。

translations.literal: At thirteen he received the capping ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he underwent the capping ceremony of adulthood.

sentences.zh: 好讀史傳，尤愛弓馬。

translations.literal: He loved reading histories and biographies, and was especially fond of archery and horsemanship.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in historical texts and had a particular passion for archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 及長，美鬚眉，大眼方口，長七尺四寸。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he had handsome brows and beard, large eyes and a square mouth, and stood seven chi four cun tall.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood, he was strikingly handsome—fine brows and beard, large eyes, a square mouth—and stood seven feet four inches in height.

sentences.zh: 親覽宮事，延接賓客，意之所欲，上必從之。

translations.literal: He personally reviewed palace affairs and received guests; whatever he wished, the emperor invariably granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He took personal charge of palace business and received guests freely; whatever he desired, the emperor invariably granted.

sentences.zh: 東宮置兵，與羽林等。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace was given troops equal to the Feathered Forest guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace was outfitted with troops rivaling the imperial Feathered Forest guard.

sentences.zh: 十七年，劭拜京陵，大將軍彭城王義康、竟陵王誕、尚書桂陽侯義融並從，司空江夏王義恭自江都來會京口。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Shao paid homage at the imperial tombs; Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, Prince of Jingling Dan, and Minister of the Masters of Writing Marquis of Guiyang Yirong all accompanied him, while Minister of Works Prince of Jiangxia Yigong came from Jiangdu to meet them at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Shao performed rites at the imperial tombs. Grand General Yikang, Prince of Pengcheng, Prince of Jingling Dan, and Minister of the Masters of Writing Yirong, Marquis of Guiyang, all accompanied him, while Minister of Works Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, came from Jiangdu to join them at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，上將北伐，劭與蕭思話固諫，不從。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, when the emperor was about to launch a northern campaign, Shao and Xiao Sihua firmly remonstrated, but he would not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, as the emperor prepared a northern expedition, Shao and Xiao Sihua remonstrated firmly, but he would not be persuaded.

sentences.zh: 索虜至瓜步，京邑震駭。

translations.literal: The northern barbarians reached Guabu, and the capital was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Wei reached Guabu, the capital convulsed with fear.

sentences.zh: 劭出鎮石頭，總統水軍。

translations.literal: Shao went out to garrison Shitou and took overall command of the river forces.
translations.idiomatic: Shao took command at Shitou Fortress and assumed overall direction of the river fleet.

sentences.zh: 善於撫禦。

translations.literal: He was skilled at comforting and controlling the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He showed a gift for rallying and commanding the men.

sentences.zh: 上登石頭城，有憂色，劭曰：「不斬江湛、徐湛之，無以謝天下。」

translations.literal: The emperor ascended Shitou fortress with a troubled look. Shao said, "Unless Jiang Zhan and Xu Zhanzhi are beheaded, there is no way to answer to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor climbed Shitou fortress, worry clouded his face. Shao said, "Unless we execute Jiang Zhan and Xu Zhanzhi, we cannot answer to the realm."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「北伐自我意，不關二人也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The northern campaign was my own decision—it has nothing to do with those two men."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "The northern campaign was my decision alone—it has nothing to do with those two."

sentences.zh: 上時務在本業，勸課耕桑，使宮內皆蠶，欲以諷厲天下。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor devoted himself to fundamental industry, encouraging farming and sericulture, and made everyone within the palace raise silkworms, wishing thereby to admonish and inspire the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then devoted himself to the fundamentals of statecraft, urging farming and sericulture and requiring everyone within the palace to raise silkworms, hoping to set an example for the realm.

sentences.zh: 有女巫嚴道育，本吳興人，自言通靈，能役使鬼物。

translations.literal: There was a shamaness named Yan Daoyu, a native of Wuxing, who claimed spiritual communion and the ability to command ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: A shamaness named Yan Daoyu, originally from Wuxing, claimed supernatural powers and the ability to command spirits.

sentences.zh: 夫為劫，坐沒入奚官。

translations.literal: Her husband committed robbery and, on conviction, was confiscated into the palace women’s service.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband had committed robbery and, upon conviction, was confiscated into the palace women’s bureau.

sentences.zh: 劭姊東陽公主應閣婢王鸚鵡白公主雲：「道育通靈有異術。」

translations.literal: Shao's elder sister, the Princess of Dongyang, had a maid of the inner gate named Wang Yingwu who told the princess, "Daoyu communes with spirits and possesses extraordinary arts."
translations.idiomatic: Shao's elder sister, the Princess of Dongyang, had a maid of the inner gate named Wang Yingwu who told her, "Daoyu communes with spirits and commands extraordinary arts."

sentences.zh: 主乃白上，托雲善蠶，求召入，見許。

translations.literal: The princess then reported to the emperor, alleging skill in sericulture, and requested that she be summoned in; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The princess reported to the emperor, claiming Daoyu was skilled at sericulture, and asked that she be summoned to court; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 道育既入，自言服食，主及劭並信惑之。

translations.literal: Once Daoyu had entered, she declared herself adept at ingesting elixirs; the princess and Shao alike were deluded into believing her.
translations.idiomatic: After Daoyu entered the palace, she claimed expertise in elixir practices, and both the princess and Shao fell under her spell.

sentences.zh: 始興王浚素佞事劭，與劭並多過失，慮上知，使道育祈請，欲令過不上聞。

translations.literal: Prince of Shixing Jun had long fawned upon Shao; he and Shao alike had many faults and, fearing the emperor might learn of them, had Daoyu offer prayers, wishing their offenses would not reach the emperor's ears.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shixing Jun had long curried favor with Shao; both had many transgressions to hide and, fearing the emperor might learn of them, enlisted Daoyu to pray that their faults would never reach his ears.

sentences.zh: 道育輒雲：「自上天陳請，必不洩露。」

translations.literal: Daoyu would always say, "I myself present the petition in Heaven above; it will certainly not be disclosed."
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu would always assure them, "I present your petitions in Heaven above—they will never be disclosed."

sentences.zh: 劭等敬事，號曰天師。

translations.literal: Shao and the others honored her in service and called her the Celestial Master.
translations.idiomatic: Shao and the others venerated her and addressed her as the Celestial Master.

sentences.zh: 後遂為巫蠱，以玉人為上形像，埋于含章殿前。

translations.literal: Later they turned to witchcraft sorcery, fashioning a jade figure in the emperor's likeness and burying it before the Hanzhang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: They then practiced witchcraft sorcery, carving a jade effigy of the emperor and burying it before the Hanzhang Hall.

sentences.zh: 初，東陽主有奴陳天興，鸚鵡養以為子，而與之淫通。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Princess of Dongyang had a slave named Chen Tianxing whom Yingwu raised as her son and with whom she had illicit relations.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Princess of Dongyang had owned a slave named Chen Tianxing; Yingwu had raised him as her son and carried on an illicit affair with him.

sentences.zh: 鸚鵡、天興及寧州所獻黃門慶國並預巫蠱事。

translations.literal: Yingwu, Tianxing, and Qing Guo, a Yellow Gate eunuch presented by Ningzhou, all took part in the witchcraft affair.
translations.idiomatic: Yingwu, Tianxing, and Qing Guo—a eunuch of the Yellow Gate presented by Ningzhou—all participated in the witchcraft plot.

sentences.zh: 劭以天興補隊主。

translations.literal: Shao appointed Tianxing to fill a squad-leader post.
translations.idiomatic: Shao installed Tianxing as a squad leader.

sentences.zh: 東陽主薨，鸚鵡應出嫁，劭慮言語難密，與浚謀之。

translations.literal: When the Princess of Dongyang died, Yingwu was due to be married off; Shao feared her tongue could not be kept secret and plotted with Jun.
translations.idiomatic: After the Princess of Dongyang died, Yingwu was to be married off; Shao feared she could not keep secrets and consulted Jun.

sentences.zh: 時吳興沈懷遠為浚府佐，見待異常，乃嫁鸚鵡與懷遠為妾，不以啟上，慮後事泄，因臨賀公主微言之。

translations.literal: At that time Shen Huaiyuan of Wuxing was a staff officer in Jun's household and was treated with exceptional favor; they therefore married Yingwu to Huaiyuan as a concubine without reporting it to the emperor, fearing the matter might later leak out, and dropped a hint to the Princess of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiyuan of Wuxing was then an officer on Jun's staff and enjoyed unusual favor; they married Yingwu to him as a concubine without informing the emperor, fearing exposure later, and let the Princess of Linhe hear a veiled hint of it.

sentences.zh: 上後知天興領隊，遣閹人奚承祖詰讓劭曰：「臨賀公主南第先有一下人欲嫁，又聞此下人養他人奴為兒，而汝用為隊主，抽拔何乃速。

translations.literal: The emperor later learned that Tianxing was leading a squad and sent the eunuch Xi Chengzu to rebuke Shao, saying, "The Princess of Linhe's southern residence already had a servant girl who wished to marry, and I further hear that this servant raised another person's slave as her son—yet you made him a squad leader. Why such haste in promoting him?
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor later learned Tianxing was leading a squad, he sent the eunuch Xi Chengzu to rebuke Shao: "The Princess of Linhe's southern residence already had a servant who wished to marry, and I hear this servant raised another man's slave as her son—yet you made him squad leader. Why promote him so quickly?

sentences.zh: 汝間用主、副，並是奴邪？

translations.literal: Are the leaders and deputies you employ from time to time all slaves?
translations.idiomatic: Are the squad leaders and deputies you appoint all slaves?

sentences.zh: 欲嫁置何處？」

translations.literal: Where do you intend to place the one who wishes to marry?"
translations.idiomatic: Where do you intend to place the servant who wishes to marry?"

sentences.zh: 劭答曰：「南第昔屬天興，求將驅使，臣答曰：'伍那可得，若能擊賊者，可入隊。

translations.literal: Shao replied, "The southern residence once belonged to Tianxing; he asked to be taken for service. Your servant answered, 'How could a common soldier be obtained? If he can strike down enemies, he may enter the squad.
translations.idiomatic: Shao replied, "The southern residence once fell under Tianxing's charge; he asked to serve under me. I answered, 'A common soldier cannot simply be taken—if he can fight, he may join the squad.

sentences.zh: '當時蓋戲言耳，都不復憶。

translations.literal: That was merely jesting talk at the time; I no longer remember it at all.
translations.idiomatic: That was only a jest at the time; I had entirely forgotten it.

sentences.zh: 後天興道上通辭乞位，追存往為者，不忍食言，呼視見其形容粗健，堪充驅使，脫爾使監禮兼隊副。

translations.literal: Later Tianxing met me on the road and presented a petition begging for a post; recalling what had been said before, I could not bear to break my word. I summoned and inspected him—his build was rugged and strong, fit for service—and on the spur of the moment made him overseer of ritual observance and also squad deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tianxing intercepted me on the road and begged for a post; remembering my earlier words, I could not break my promise. I summoned him, saw he was sturdily built and fit for service, and on impulse made him overseer of ritual observance and squad deputy.

sentences.zh: 比用人雖取勞舊，亦參用有氣幹者。

translations.literal: In appointing men recently, although I draw on those with long service, I also mix in men of spirit and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: In recent appointments I have drawn on veterans of long service, but I also include men of proven mettle.

sentences.zh: 謹條牒人囗名上呈。

translations.literal: I respectfully submit a roster listing the men's names for presentation above.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit a roster of their names for your review.

sentences.zh: 下人欲嫁者，猶未有處。」

translations.literal: As for the servant girl who wishes to marry, there is as yet no place arranged."
translations.idiomatic: As for the servant who wishes to marry, no arrangement has yet been made."

sentences.zh: 時鸚鵡已嫁懷遠矣。

translations.literal: By then Yingwu had already been married to Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yingwu had already been married to Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 劭懼，馳書告浚，並使報臨賀主：「上若問嫁處，當言未有定所。」

translations.literal: Shao was afraid and sent a hurried letter informing Jun, and also had the Princess of Linhe told: "If the emperor asks where the marriage is to be placed, you must say no fixed place has been decided."
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Shao sent an urgent letter to Jun and instructed the Princess of Linhe: "If the emperor asks where the marriage is arranged, say no decision has been made."

sentences.zh: 浚答書曰：「奉令，伏深惶怖，啟此事多日，今始來問，當是有感發之者，未測源由爾。

translations.literal: Jun replied in a letter: "I have received your order and am prostrate with deep fear. This matter was raised many days ago; that inquiry comes only now suggests something has stirred him—I cannot yet fathom the source.
translations.idiomatic: Jun wrote back: "Your order received—I am prostrate with fear. This matter was broached days ago; that he asks only now means something must have stirred him, though I cannot yet trace the source.

sentences.zh: 計臨賀故當不應翻覆言語，自生寒熱也。

translations.literal: I reckon the Princess of Linhe ought not to have reversed her story in speech—she has brought this chill and fever upon herself.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Linhe should not have changed her story—that is what brought this trouble on herself.

sentences.zh: 此姥由來挾兩端，難可孤保，正爾自問臨賀，冀得審實也。

translations.literal: This old woman has always played both sides; she is hard to trust alone. It is just as well to question the Princess of Linhe yourself, hoping to obtain the truth.
translations.idiomatic: That old woman has always played both sides and cannot be trusted alone. You should question the Princess of Linhe yourself to learn the truth.

sentences.zh: 其若見問，當作依違答之。

translations.literal: If she is questioned, she should answer evasively.
translations.idiomatic: If she is questioned, she should answer evasively.

sentences.zh: 天興先署佞人府位，不審監上當無此簿領爾。

translations.literal: Tianxing was earlier posted to a position in the sycophant's household—I do not know whether the overseer's office above will have this on its registers.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxing was once posted to a position in the sycophant's household—I doubt the overseer's office still has that on its registers.

sentences.zh: 急宜犍之。

translations.literal: He should be shackled at once.
translations.idiomatic: He must be shackled immediately.

sentences.zh: 殿下已見王未？

translations.literal: Has Your Highness already seen Wang?
translations.idiomatic: Have you already seen Wang?

sentences.zh: 宜依此具令嚴自躬上啟聞。

translations.literal: You should follow this fully and have Yan report it in person to Heaven above.
translations.idiomatic: Follow this fully and have Yan report it in person to the spirits above.

sentences.zh: 彼人若為不已，正可促其餘命，或是大慶之漸。」

translations.literal: If that man will not stop, you may just hasten what life remains to him—or it may be the beginning of great rejoicing."
translations.idiomatic: If that man will not relent, you may simply shorten what life remains to him—or it may herald great fortune."

sentences.zh: 凡劭、浚相與書疏類如此，所言皆為名號，謂上為「彼人」，或以為「其人」；

translations.literal: In general the letters exchanged between Shao and Jun were all of this sort; what they said used code names, calling the emperor "that man" or sometimes "the man";
translations.idiomatic: Letters between Shao and Jun were generally written in this vein, using code names: the emperor was "that man" or sometimes "the man";

sentences.zh: 以太尉江夏王義恭為「佞人」；

translations.literal: they called Grand Commandant Prince of Jiangxia Yigong "the sycophant";
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, was "the sycophant";

sentences.zh: 東陽主第在西掖門外，故雲「南第」，王即鸚鵡姓，躬上啟聞者，令道育上天白天神也。

translations.literal: the Princess of Dongyang's residence lay outside the Western Corner Gate, hence they said "southern residence"; Wang was Yingwu's surname; "report in person to Heaven above" meant having Daoyu ascend to inform the celestial spirits.
translations.idiomatic: the Princess of Dongyang's residence lay outside the Western Corner Gate, hence "southern residence"; Wang was Yingwu's surname; and "report in person above" meant having Daoyu ascend to inform the celestial spirits.

sentences.zh: 鸚鵡既適懷遠，慮與天興私通事泄，請劭殺之。

translations.literal: Once Yingwu had been given in marriage to Huaiyuan, she feared the affair with Tianxing might leak out and asked Shao to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: After Yingwu married Huaiyuan, she feared their affair with Tianxing might be exposed and begged Shao to kill him.

sentences.zh: 劭密使人害天興。

translations.literal: Shao secretly sent men to kill Tianxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shao secretly had Tianxing murdered.

sentences.zh: 慶國謂宣傳往來，唯有二人，天興既死，慮將見及，乃具以其事白上。

translations.literal: Qing Guo reckoned that of those who carried messages back and forth, only two men remained; with Tianxing dead, he feared he would be implicated next and therefore reported the whole affair in detail to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Guo knew only two men still carried messages between the conspirators; with Tianxing dead, he feared he would be next and reported everything to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上驚惋，即遣收鸚鵡，封籍其家，得劭、浚書數百紙，皆咒詛巫蠱之言，得所埋上形像于宮內。

translations.literal: The emperor was shocked and grieved; he immediately sent to seize Yingwu and seal her household for inventory, obtaining several hundred sheets of letters from Shao and Jun—all words of cursing and witchcraft sorcery—and recovered within the palace the buried image of the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was shocked and grieved. He immediately seized Yingwu and sealed her household, recovering several hundred letters from Shao and Jun filled with curses and witchcraft, and unearthed within the palace the buried effigy of the emperor.

sentences.zh: 道育叛亡，討捕不得。

translations.literal: Daoyu rebelled and fled; pursuit and capture failed.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu fled and could not be captured.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，窮治其事，分遣中使入東諸郡搜討，遂不獲。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and prosecuted the case to the utmost, dispatching palace envoys into the eastern commanderies to search and pursue, yet she was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and prosecuted the case exhaustively, sending palace envoys through the eastern commanderies to hunt her down, but she was never found.

sentences.zh: 上詰責劭、浚，劭、浚惶懼無辭，唯陳謝而已。

translations.literal: The emperor interrogated and rebuked Shao and Jun; Shao and Jun were fearful and had no words, offering only apologies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor interrogated and rebuked Shao and Jun; terrified and speechless, they could only beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 道育變服為尼，逃匿東宮，浚往京口，又載以自隨，或出止民張旿家。

translations.literal: Daoyu changed her dress and became a nun, hiding in the Eastern Palace; when Jun went to Jingkou he again carried her with him, or would lodge at the home of the commoner Zhang Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu disguised herself as a nun and hid in the Eastern Palace; when Jun went to Jingkou he took her along again, sometimes lodging at the home of a commoner named Zhang Xu.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭自盱眙還朝，上以巫蠱告之，曰：「常見典籍有此，謂之書傳空言，不意遂所親睹。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jiangxia Yigong returned to court from Xuyi, the emperor informed him of the witchcraft affair, saying, "I have often seen this in the classics and called it empty talk in books and traditions—I never expected to witness it with my own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: When Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, returned from Xuyi, the emperor told him of the witchcraft plot, saying, "I had often read of such things in the classics and dismissed them as empty tradition—I never expected to see it with my own eyes.

sentences.zh: 劭雖所行失道，未必便亡社稷，南面之日，非複我及汝事。

translations.literal: Although Shao's conduct has lost the Way, the altars of state may not necessarily perish at once; once he faces south upon the throne, it will no longer be a matter for you and me.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shao has lost the Way, the dynasty may not fall immediately; once he faces south as emperor, it will no longer be our affair.

sentences.zh: 汝兒子多，將來遇此不幸爾。」

translations.literal: You have many sons—in the future they may meet this misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: You have many sons—they may yet suffer this misfortune in their turn."

sentences.zh: 先是二十八年，彗星起畢、昴，入太微，掃帝座端門，滅翼、軫。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the twenty-eighth year, a comet rose in Bi and Mao, entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure, swept the Imperial Seat and the Upright Gate, and extinguished Yi and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the twenty-eighth year, a comet rose in the Net and Hairy Head constellations, entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure, swept the Imperial Seat and the Upright Gate, and passed through the Wings and Chariot constellations.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，熒惑逆行守氐，自十一月霖雨連雪，太陽罕曜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Mars moved retrograde and guarded Di; from the eleventh month onward continuous rain and snow fell, and the sun rarely shone.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Mars moved retrograde and held station at Di; from the eleventh month onward rain and snow fell without cease, and the sun rarely appeared.

sentences.zh: 三十年正月，大風飛霰且雷。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirtieth year, great winds drove flying sleet and thunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirtieth year, fierce winds drove sleet and thunder across the sky.

sentences.zh: 上憂有竊發，輒加劭兵眾，東宮實甲萬人。

translations.literal: The emperor feared a covert rising and repeatedly increased Shao's troops; the Eastern Palace in fact had ten thousand men under arms.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a covert coup, the emperor repeatedly augmented Shao's forces until the Eastern Palace mustered ten thousand armed men.

sentences.zh: 車駕出行，劭入守，使將白直隊自隨。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went out, Shao entered to guard the palace and had the white-uniform direct guard accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor traveled abroad, Shao entered the palace to guard it and kept the white-uniform direct guard at his side.

sentences.zh: 其年二月，浚自京口入朝，當鎮江陵，複載道育還東宮，欲將西上。

translations.literal: In the second month of that year Jun entered court from Jingkou; he was due to garrison Jiangling, again carried Daoyu back to the Eastern Palace, and intended to take her west with him.
translations.idiomatic: That second month Jun came to court from Jingkou before taking up his post at Jiangling; he brought Daoyu back to the Eastern Palace again, intending to take her west with him.

sentences.zh: 有告上雲：「京口民張旿家有一尼，服食，出入征北內，似是嚴道育。」

translations.literal: Someone reported to the emperor, "At the home of the Jingkou commoner Zhang Xu there is a nun who ingests elixirs and goes in and out within the Northern Campaigning Prince's quarters—she appears to be Yan Daoyu."
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported to the emperor, "At the home of Zhang Xu, a commoner in Jingkou, there is a nun who takes elixirs and enters the Northern Campaigning Prince's residence—it may be Yan Daoyu."

sentences.zh: 上初不信，試使掩錄，得其二婢，雲：「道育隨征北還都。」

translations.literal: At first the emperor did not believe it; he tried sending men to seize and question them, obtaining her two maidservants, who said, "Daoyu returned to the capital with the Northern Campaigning Prince."
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor disbelieved; he sent men to seize and question them, capturing two maidservants who said, "Daoyu returned to the capital with the Northern Campaigning Prince."

sentences.zh: 上謂劭、浚已當斥遣道育，而猶與往來，惆悵惋駭。

translations.literal: The emperor thought Shao and Jun ought already to have dismissed Daoyu, yet they still associated with her—he was filled with sorrow, regret, and alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed Shao and Jun should already have banished Daoyu; that they still kept company with her left him stricken with sorrow and alarm.

sentences.zh: 乃使京口以船送道育二婢，須至檢核，廢劭，賜浚死，以語浚母潘淑妃，淑妃具以告浚。

translations.literal: He then had Jingkou send Daoyu's two maidservants by boat; once they arrived for examination he would depose Shao and grant Jun death. He spoke of this to Jun's mother, Consort Pan the Cultivated, and the consort reported it all to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jingkou to send Daoyu's two maidservants by boat; once they arrived for interrogation he would depose Shao and order Jun to take his own life. He confided this to Jun's mother, Consort Pan the Cultivated, who told Jun everything.

sentences.zh: 浚馳報劭，劭因是異謀，每夜輒饗將士，或親自行酒，密與腹心隊主陳叔兒、詹叔兒、齋帥張超之、任建之謀之。

translations.literal: Jun sent a hurried report to Shao; Shao therefore formed a different plot, every night feasting the officers or personally going among them with wine, secretly plotting with his trusted squad leaders Chen Shuer and Zhan Shuer, fast-guard commander Zhang Chaozhi, and Ren Jianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent urgent word to Shao, who thereupon formed a new plot. Each night he feasted his officers, sometimes serving wine himself, and secretly conspired with his trusted squad leaders Chen Shuer and Zhan Shuer, fast-guard commander Zhang Chaozhi, and Ren Jianzhi.

sentences.zh: 道育婢將至，其月二十一日夜，詐上詔雲：「魯秀謀反，汝可平明守闕，率眾入。」

translations.literal: When Daoyu's maidservants were about to arrive, on the night of the twenty-first day of that month he forged an imperial edict saying, "Lu Xiu is plotting rebellion—you may at dawn guard the gate towers and lead the masses in."
translations.idiomatic: As Daoyu's maidservants were nearing arrival, on the night of the twenty-first he forged an imperial edict: "Lu Xiu is plotting rebellion—at dawn guard the gate towers and lead your men inside."

sentences.zh: 因使超之等集素所畜養兵士二千余人，皆使被甲，召內外幢隊主副，豫加部勒，雲有所討。

translations.literal: He then had Chaozhi and the others assemble more than two thousand soldiers he had long kept and trained, all ordered to don armor; he summoned the leaders and deputies of the inner and outer banner squads, gave them advance orders, and declared there was something to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: He had Chaozhi and the others muster more than two thousand soldiers he had long kept in training, all armored, and summoned the inner and outer banner squad leaders, telling them a punitive action was at hand.

sentences.zh: 宿召前中庶子、右軍長史蕭斌，夜呼斌及左衛率袁淑、中舍人殷仲素、左積弩將軍王正見，併入宮，告以大事，自起拜斌等，因流涕，眾並驚愕，語在淑傳。

translations.literal: He had earlier summoned the former palace attendant, Right Army Chief Clerk Xiao Bin; that night he called Bin, Left Guard Commander Yuan Shu, Palace Attendant Yin Zhongsu, and Left Strong Crossbow General Wang Zhengjian, all entering the palace together, and informed them of the great affair; he himself rose to bow to Bin and the others and wept; all were shocked—the account is in Shu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: He had already summoned the former palace attendant and Right Army chief clerk Xiao Bin; that night he called in Bin, Left Guard Commander Yuan Shu, palace attendant Yin Zhongsu, and Left Strong Crossbow General Wang Zhengjian, told them of the coup, rose to bow to them in tears, and left them all stunned—the full account appears in Shu's biography.

sentences.zh: 明旦未開鼓，劭以硃服加戎服上，乘畫輪車，與蕭斌同載，衛從如常入朝之儀，守門開，從萬春門入。

translations.literal: At dawn, before the drums opened the gates, Shao wore vermilion robes over military dress, rode in a painted-wheel carriage sharing the carriage with Xiao Bin, with guards and followers as in the usual court entry ritual; the gatekeepers opened the gates and he entered through the Wanchun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, before the gate drums sounded, Shao wore vermilion robes over armor, rode in a painted carriage with Xiao Bin, and entered with his usual court escort through the opened Wanchun Gate.

sentences.zh: 舊制，東宮隊不得入城，劭與門衛雲：「受敕，有所收討。」

translations.literal: By old regulation the Eastern Palace troops might not enter the city; Shao told the gate guards, "I have received an edict—there is something to be seized and punished."
translations.idiomatic: By regulation Eastern Palace troops could not enter the city; Shao told the gate guards, "I have received an edict to conduct a punitive seizure."

sentences.zh: 令後隊速來，張超之等數十人馳入雲龍、東中華門及齋閣，拔刀徑上合殿。

translations.literal: He ordered the rear squads to come quickly; Chaozhi and several dozen others galloped through the Cloud Dragon Gate, the Eastern Central Splendor Gate, and the fasting chambers, drawing swords and going straight up to the Unified Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the rear squads to follow quickly. Chaozhi and several dozen men galloped through the Cloud Dragon Gate, the Eastern Central Splendor Gate, and the fasting chambers, swords drawn, straight to the Unified Hall.

sentences.zh: 上其夜與尚書僕射徐湛之屏人語，至旦燭猶未滅，直衛兵尚寢。

translations.literal: That night the emperor was speaking with Minister of the Masters of Writing Xu Zhanzhi behind screened attendants; by dawn the candles were still not extinguished, and the direct guards were still asleep.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor had been speaking privately with Xu Zhanzhi, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing; at dawn the candles still burned and the direct guards still slept.

sentences.zh: 超之手行弑逆，並殺湛之。

translations.literal: Chaozhi personally carried out the regicide and also killed Zhanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozhi murdered the emperor with his own hand and killed Zhanzhi as well.

sentences.zh: 劭進至合殿中閣，太祖已崩，出坐東堂，蕭斌執刀侍直。

translations.literal: Shao advanced to the inner bay of the Unified Hall; the Grand Ancestor had already perished. He came out and sat in the Eastern Hall while Xiao Bin held a sword standing attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Shao advanced to the inner bay of the Unified Hall. The Grand Ancestor was already dead. He emerged and took his seat in the Eastern Hall while Xiao Bin stood guard with drawn sword.

sentences.zh: 呼中書舍人顧嘏，嘏震懼不時出，既至，問曰：「欲共見廢，何不蚤啟？」

translations.literal: He summoned Palace Secretariat Attendant Gu Gu; Gu, terrified, did not come out promptly. Once he arrived, Shao asked, "You wished to see us both deposed—why did you not report it early?"
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Gu Gu, Attendant of the Palace Secretariat. Terrified, Gu delayed coming; when he arrived Shao demanded, "You wanted us deposed—why did you not warn us sooner?"

sentences.zh: 未及答，即於前斬之。

translations.literal: Before he could answer, Shao beheaded him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Before Gu could answer, Shao struck off his head on the spot.

sentences.zh: 遣人於崇禮闥殺吏部尚書江湛。

translations.literal: He sent men to kill Minister of the Masters of Writing Jiang Zhan at the Chongli Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men to kill Jiang Zhan, Minister of the Masters of Writing, at the Chongli Gate.

sentences.zh: 太祖左細杖主卜天與攻劭於東堂，見殺。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor's chief of the left fine-staff guards, Bu Tianyu, attacked Shao in the Eastern Hall and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Tianyu, chief of the Grand Ancestor's left fine-staff guards, attacked Shao in the Eastern Hall and was slain.

sentences.zh: 又使人從東閣入殺潘淑妃，又殺太祖親信左右數十人。

translations.literal: He also sent men in through the Eastern Pavilion to kill Consort Pan the Cultivated, and killed several dozen of the Grand Ancestor's trusted attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent men through the Eastern Pavilion to kill Consort Pan the Cultivated and slew several dozen of the Grand Ancestor's closest attendants.

sentences.zh: 急召始興王浚，率眾屯中堂。

translations.literal: He urgently summoned Prince of Shixing Jun to lead troops and encamp in the Central Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently summoned Jun, Prince of Shixing, to lead troops and encamp in the Central Hall.

sentences.zh: 又召太尉江夏王義恭、尚書令何尚之。

translations.literal: He also summoned Grand Commandant Prince of Jiangxia Yigong and Director of the Masters of Writing He Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He also summoned Grand Commandant Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, and Director of the Masters of Writing He Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 劭即偽位，為書曰：「徐湛之、江湛弑逆無狀，吾勒兵入殿，已無所及，號惋崩恤，肝心破裂。

translations.literal: Shao immediately usurped the throne and composed a proclamation: "Xu Zhanzhi and Jiang Zhan have committed outrageous regicide; I led troops into the hall but could not arrive in time—I wail in grief as if my liver and heart have split apart.
translations.idiomatic: Shao immediately usurped the throne and issued a proclamation: "Xu Zhanzhi and Jiang Zhan have committed outrageous regicide. I led troops into the hall but arrived too late—I wail in grief as though my heart were torn apart.

sentences.zh: 今罪人斯得，元兇克殄，可大赦天下。

translations.literal: Now the culprits have been obtained and the primary villain extinguished—a great amnesty may be proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The culprits are now in hand and the primary villain destroyed—a great amnesty is proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 改元嘉三十年為太初元年。

translations.literal: The thirtieth year of Yuanjia is changed to the first year of Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: The thirtieth year of Yuanjia is renamed the first year of Taichu.

sentences.zh: 文武並賜位二等，諸科一依丁卯。」

translations.literal: Civil and military officials alike were granted two ranks of promotion; all categories followed the Dingmao precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials alike were promoted two ranks; all other measures followed the Dingmao precedent."

sentences.zh: 初，使蕭斌作詔，斌辭以不文，乃使侍中王僧綽為之。

translations.literal: Earlier he had ordered Xiao Bin to draft the edict; Bin declined on grounds of literary inadequacy, so Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Sengchuo was ordered to compose it.
translations.idiomatic: He had first ordered Xiao Bin to draft the edict, but Bin pleaded literary inadequacy, so Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Sengchuo was commissioned instead.

sentences.zh: 使改元為太初，劭素與道育所定。

translations.literal: He ordered the era name changed to Taichu—something Shao had long ago settled with Daoyu.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the era name changed to Taichu—a name Shao had long ago chosen with Daoyu.

sentences.zh: 斌曰：「舊逾年改元。」

translations.literal: Bin said, "By old custom the era name is changed only after the year has passed."
translations.idiomatic: Bin objected, "By custom the era name is changed only after the year has turned."

sentences.zh: 劭以問僧綽，繒綽曰：「晉惠帝即位，便改號。」

translations.literal: Shao asked Sengchuo about it; Sengchuo said, "When Emperor Hui of Jin took the throne, he changed the era name at once."
translations.idiomatic: Shao consulted Sengchuo, who replied, "When Emperor Hui of Jin ascended the throne, he changed the era name immediately."

sentences.zh: 劭喜而從之。

translations.literal: Shao was pleased and followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Shao followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 百僚至者裁數十人，劭便遽即位。

translations.literal: Of the hundred officials only several dozen had arrived; Shao thereupon hastened to take the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Only a few dozen officials had arrived, yet Shao hastened to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 即位畢，稱疾還入永福省，然後遷大行皇帝升太極前殿。

translations.literal: When the enthronement was complete he claimed illness and returned to the Yongfu Bureau, only then having the late emperor's coffin moved up to the front hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned he feigned illness and withdrew to the Yongfu Bureau, then had the late emperor's coffin moved to the front hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 是日，以蕭斌為散騎常侍、尚書僕射、領軍將軍；

translations.literal: That day Xiao Bin was made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, and General Who Leads the Army;
translations.idiomatic: That day Xiao Bin was appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, and General Who Leads the Army;

sentences.zh: 何尚之為司空；

translations.literal: He Shangzhi was made Minister of Works;
translations.idiomatic: He Shangzhi was made Minister of Works;

sentences.zh: 前右衛率檀和之戍石頭；

translations.literal: former Right Guard Commander Tan Hezhi garrisoned Shitou;
translations.idiomatic: former Right Guard Commander Tan Hezhi garrisoned Shitou;

sentences.zh: 侍中營道侯義綦為征虜將軍、晉陵南下邳二郡太守，鎮京城；

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Marquis of Yingdao Yiqi was made General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Administrator of Jinling and Xiapi in the two southern commanderies, garrisoning the capital region;
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Yiqi, Marquis of Yingdao, was made General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and administrator of Jinling and Xiapi, garrisoning the capital region;

sentences.zh: 尚書殷仲景為侍中、中護軍。

translations.literal: Minister of the Masters of Writing Yin Zhongjing was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Central Army Protector.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongjing, Minister of the Masters of Writing, was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Central Army Protector.

sentences.zh: 大行皇帝大斂，劭辭疾不敢出。

translations.literal: At the great encoffinment of the late emperor, Shao pleaded illness and dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: At the late emperor's great encoffinment, Shao pleaded illness and dared not appear.

sentences.zh: 先給諸王及諸處兵杖，悉收還武庫。

translations.literal: Weapons earlier issued to the princes and to various posts were all recalled to the armory.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons previously issued to the princes and regional garrisons were all recalled to the armory.

sentences.zh: 殺徐湛之、江湛親黨新除始興內史荀赤松、新除尚書左丞臧凝之、山陰令傅僧祐、吳令江徽、前征北行參軍諸葛詡、右衛司馬江文綱。

translations.literal: He killed the kinsmen and associates of Xu Zhanzhi and Jiang Zhan: the newly appointed Interior Minister of Shixing Xun Chisong, the newly appointed Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Zang Ningzhi, the magistrate of Shanyin Fu Sengyou, the magistrate of Wu Jiang Hui, former Northern Campaigning Army acting staff officer Zhuge Xu, and Right Guard Major Jiang Wengang.
translations.idiomatic: He executed the kinsmen and associates of Xu Zhanzhi and Jiang Zhan, including the newly appointed interior minister of Shixing Xun Chisong, the newly appointed left assistant director Zang Ningzhi, the magistrates of Shanyin and Wu, former northern campaign staff officer Zhuge Xu, and Right Guard major Jiang Wengang.

sentences.zh: 以殷仲素為黃門侍郎，王正見為左軍將軍，張超之及諸同逆聞人文子、徐興祖、詹叔兒、陳叔兒、任建之等，並將校以下龍驤將軍帶郡，各賜錢二十萬。

translations.literal: Yin Zhongsu was made Yellow Gate Attendant-Cadet and Wang Zhengjian Left Army General; Zhang Chaozhi and the fellow conspirators Wen Renzi, Xu Xingzu, Zhan Shuer, Chen Shuer, Ren Jianzhi, and others—all commanders and below—were made Dragon-Prancing Generals with nominal commandery affiliation, each granted two hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongsu was made Attendant-Cadet of the Yellow Gate and Wang Zhengjian Left Army General; Zhang Chaozhi and fellow conspirators Wen Renzi, Xu Xingzu, Zhan Shuer, Chen Shuer, and Ren Jianzhi were all promoted to Dragon-Prancing General with nominal commandery titles and granted two hundred thousand cash each.

sentences.zh: 遣人謂魯秀曰：「徐湛之常欲相危，我已為卿除之矣。」

translations.literal: He sent someone to tell Lu Xiu, "Xu Zhanzhi always wished to endanger you—I have already removed him for your sake."
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to Lu Xiu: "Xu Zhanzhi always meant you harm—I have already removed him for you."

sentences.zh: 使秀與屯騎校尉龐秀之對掌軍隊。

translations.literal: He had Xiu and Commandant of Agile Cavalry Pang Xiuzhi jointly command the armies.
translations.idiomatic: He paired Xiu with Commandant of Agile Cavalry Pang Xiuzhi to jointly command the armies.

sentences.zh: 以侍中王僧綽為吏部尚書，司徒左長史何偃為侍中。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Sengchuo was made Minister of the Masters of Writing for Personnel, and the Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education He Yan was made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengchuo was promoted from Attendant-in-Ordinary to Minister of Personnel, and He Yan, left chief clerk of the Minister of Education, was made Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 成服日，劭登殿臨靈，號慟不自持。

translations.literal: On the day mourning garments were completed, Shao ascended the hall to face the coffin and wailed until he could not control himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning garments were completed, Shao ascended the hall before the coffin and wailed until he could no longer control himself.

sentences.zh: 博訪公卿，詢求治道，薄賦輕徭，損諸游費。

translations.literal: He broadly consulted the high ministers, inquiring after the way of governance, lightening taxes and corvée labor, and reducing various recreational expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: He consulted widely among the high ministers on governance, lightened taxes and corvée labor, and cut recreational expenditures.

sentences.zh: 田苑山澤，有可弛者，假與貧民。

translations.literal: Fields, parks, mountains, and marshes that could be released were lent to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial fields, parks, and wetlands that could be released were lent to the poor.

sentences.zh: 三月，遣大使分行四方，分浙以東五郡為會州，省揚州立司隸校尉，以殷沖補之。

translations.literal: In the third month he dispatched grand envoys to tour the four quarters; the five commanderies east of Zhe were divided off as Huizhou; Yang province was abolished and the Director of Retainers established, with Yin Chong appointed to fill the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he dispatched grand envoys throughout the realm, carved five commanderies east of Zhe into Huizhou, abolished Yang province in favor of a Director of Retainers post, and appointed Yin Chong to it.

sentences.zh: 以大將軍江夏王義恭為太保，司徒南譙王義宣為太尉，衛將軍、荊州刺史始興王浚進號驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Grand General Prince of Jiangxia Yigong was made Grand Tutor; Minister of Education Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan was made Grand Commandant; Guard General and Inspector of Jingzhou Prince of Shixing Jun was advanced in rank to Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, was made Grand Tutor; Minister of Education Yixuan, Prince of Nanqiao, was made Grand Commandant; and Guard General Jun, Prince of Shixing and inspector of Jingzhou, was promoted to Rapid Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 王僧綽以先預廢立，見誅。

translations.literal: Wang Sengchuo, because he had earlier been involved in the question of deposition and enthronement, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengchuo was executed because he had earlier been involved in deliberations over deposition and succession.

sentences.zh: 長沙王瑾、瑾弟楷、臨川王燁、桂陽侯覬、新諭侯球，並以宿恨下獄死。

translations.literal: Prince of Changsha Jin, Jin's younger brother Kai, Prince of Linchuan Ye, Marquis of Guiyang Yi, and Marquis of Xinyu Qiu—all because of old resentments—were cast into prison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Changsha Jin, his brother Kai, Prince of Linchuan Ye, Marquis of Guiyang Yi, and Marquis of Xinyu Qiu were all imprisoned and killed over old grudges.

sentences.zh: 禮官希旨，諡太祖不敢盡美稱，上諡曰中宗景皇帝。

translations.literal: The ritual officials curried favor and, in posthumously honoring the Grand Ancestor, dared not use the fullest praise; the title submitted was Emperor Jing of the Middle Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials currying favor dared not grant the Grand Ancestor full posthumous honors, submitting instead the title Emperor Jing of the Middle Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 以雍州刺史臧質為丹陽尹，進世祖號征南將軍，加散騎常侍，撫軍將軍南平王鑠中軍將軍，會稽太守隨王誕會州刺史。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yongzhou Zang Zhi was made Intendant of Danyang; the Heir Apparent was advanced to General Who Campaigns South and given the additional office of Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry; Pacification Army General Prince of Nanping Shuo was made Central Army General; and Administrator of Kuaiji Prince of Sui Dan was made Inspector of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi, inspector of Yongzhou, was made intendant of Danyang; the heir apparent was promoted to General Who Campaigns South with the additional title Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry; Shuo, Prince of Nanping and Pacification Army general, was made Central Army General; and Dan, Prince of Sui and administrator of Kuaiji, was made inspector of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭乙太保領大宗師，諮稟之科，依晉扶風王故事。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, as Grand Tutor, also headed the Great Lineage Master office; the regulations for consultation and reporting followed the precedent of the Prince of Fufeng under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, as Grand Tutor also headed the office of Great Lineage Master, with consultation procedures following the Jin precedent of the Prince of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 世祖及南譙王義宣、隨王誕諸方鎮並舉義兵。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent, Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan, Prince of Sui Dan, and the various regional commanders all raised righteous armies.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent, Yixuan Prince of Nanqiao, Dan Prince of Sui, and regional commanders throughout the empire all raised righteous armies.

sentences.zh: 劭聞義師大起，悉聚諸王及大臣于城內，移江夏王義恭住尚書下舍，義恭諸子住侍中下省。

translations.literal: When Shao heard that the righteous armies were rising in force, he gathered all the princes and great ministers inside the city, moved Prince of Jiangxia Yigong to lodge in the lower quarters of the Masters of Writing, and housed Yigong's sons in the lower bureau of the Attendants-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao learned the righteous armies were rising everywhere, he gathered all princes and high ministers inside the city, lodged Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, in the lower quarters of the Masters of Writing, and confined Yigong's sons in the attendants' lower bureau.

sentences.zh: 自永初元年以前，相國府入齋、傳教、給使，免軍戶，屬南彭城薛縣。

translations.literal: From before the first year of Yongchu onward, those who entered fasting service, carried edicts, or served as attendants in the Chancellor's office were exempted from military household status and attached to Xue County in southern Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: From before the first year of Yongchu, those who served in fasting observance, carried edicts, or attended in the chancellor's office were exempted from military household status and registered in Xue County of southern Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 劭下書，以中流起兵，當親率六師，觀變江介，悉召下番將吏。

translations.literal: Shao issued an edict: because forces had risen along the middle Yangzi, he would personally lead the Six Armies to observe developments along the river reaches, and summoned all officers and clerks on leave rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Shao issued an edict: with rebellion along the middle Yangzi, he would personally lead the Six Armies to observe developments on the river and summoned all officers on leave rotation.

sentences.zh: 加三吳太守軍號，置佐領兵。

translations.literal: He added military titles to the administrators of the Three Wu regions and appointed aides to lead troops.
translations.idiomatic: He granted military titles to the administrators of the Three Wu regions and appointed aides to command troops.

sentences.zh: 四月，立妻殷氏為皇后。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he installed his wife, the Lady Yin, as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he installed his wife, Lady Yin, as empress.

sentences.zh: 世祖檄京邑曰：

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent proclaimed to the capital:
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent issued a proclamation to the capital:

sentences.zh: 夫運不常隆，代有莫大之釁。

translations.literal: Fortune does not forever flourish; every age has its supreme calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune does not forever flourish; every age knows a supreme calamity.

sentences.zh: 爰自上葉，或因多難以成福，或階昏虐以兆亂，鹹由君臣義合，理悖恩離。

translations.literal: From high antiquity onward, some turned manifold hardships into blessing, others climbed through benighted cruelty to sow disorder—all because the bond between ruler and minister was sundered when principle opposed favor.
translations.idiomatic: Since high antiquity, some have turned hardship into blessing, others climbed through cruelty to sow disorder—all when the bond between ruler and minister broke and principle gave way to betrayal.

sentences.zh: 故堅冰之遘，每鐘澆末，未有以道禦世，教化明厚，而當梟鏡反噬，難發天屬者也。

translations.literal: Thus the encounter of solid ice always strikes at the season's decadent end; never before has a ruler governed the world by the Way with bright and generous teaching, only to suffer the owl and mirror turning to devour him—calamity erupting from his own flesh and blood.
translations.idiomatic: Solid ice forms at the decadent end of an age; never before has a ruler governed by the Way with enlightened teaching, only to be devoured by his own kin—calamity erupting from within the imperial family itself.

sentences.zh: 先帝聖德在位，功格區宇，明照萬國，道洽無垠，風之所被，荒隅變識；

translations.literal: The late emperor's sagely virtue on the throne reached to the corners of the realm; his brilliance illumined ten thousand states; his Way pervaded without limit; where his wind blew, the remotest corners changed their understanding;
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor ruled with sagely virtue; his achievements reached the corners of the realm, his brilliance illumined all states, his Way pervaded without limit, and where his influence reached even the remotest lands changed their ways;

sentences.zh: 仁之所動，木石開心。

translations.literal: where his benevolence moved, trees and stones opened their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: where his benevolence moved, even trees and stones were touched to the heart.

sentences.zh: 而賊劭乘藉塚嫡，夙蒙寵樹，正位東朝，禮絕君後，凶慢之情，發於齠昪，猜忍之心，成於幾立。

translations.literal: Yet the villain Shao, relying on his status as heir of the imperial tomb-line, had long enjoyed favor and elevation, held the correct place in the Eastern Palace, and received rites surpassing those due a son to his father; his fierce insolence arose in early childhood, his suspicious cruelty formed as he first stood.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the villain Shao, as legitimate heir, had long enjoyed favor, held the Eastern Palace, and received honors exceeding those due a son; his brutish insolence showed in childhood, his suspicious cruelty formed from his earliest years.

sentences.zh: 賊浚險躁無行，自幼而長，交相倚附，共逞奸回。

translations.literal: The villain Jun was treacherous, impetuous, and without conduct; from youth to maturity he and Shao leaned on each other and together gave free rein to wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: The villain Jun was treacherous and impetuous; growing up together, he and Shao leaned on each other and gave free rein to wickedness.

sentences.zh: 先旨以王室不造，家難亟結，故含蔽容隱，不彰其釁，訓誘啟告，冀能革音。

translations.literal: The late emperor, because the royal house was afflicted and family troubles pressed close, therefore concealed and covered their faults, not exposing their offenses, instructing and admonishing them in hope they might change their ways.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor, seeing the royal house afflicted and family troubles pressing close, concealed their faults and admonished them in hope they might reform.

sentences.zh: 何悟狂慝不悛，同惡相濟，肇亂巫蠱，終行弑逆，聖躬離荼毒之痛，社稷有翦墜之哀，四海崩心，人神泣血，生民以來，未聞斯禍。

translations.literal: Who could have known their mad wickedness would not repent, that evildoers would aid one another, that they would first raise witchcraft disorder and finally commit regicide—the sacred person parted from bitter torment, the altars of state faced the grief of being cut down, the four seas shattered in heart, men and spirits wept blood; since the birth of the people, such a calamity has never been heard.
translations.idiomatic: Who could have known they would not repent, that evildoers would aid one another, that they would practice witchcraft and finally commit regicide—the sacred person torn from us in agony, the altars of state in peril, the realm shattered, men and spirits weeping blood; since the birth of the people, no such calamity has been heard.

sentences.zh: 奉諱驚號，肝腦塗地，煩冤腷臆，容身無所。

translations.literal: Receiving the dire news, I cry out in shock; my liver and brain are smeared upon the ground; grief and injustice choke my breast—I have nowhere to place my body.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the dire news, I cry out in shock; grief smears my very liver and brain; injustice chokes my breast—I have nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 大將軍、諸王幽間窮省，存亡未測。

translations.literal: The Grand General and the princes are confined in dark imprisonment; whether they live or die cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand General and the princes languish in dark imprisonment; whether they live or die is unknown.

sentences.zh: 徐僕射、江尚書、袁左率，皆當世標秀，一時忠貞，或正色立朝，或聞逆弗順，並橫分階闥，懸首都市。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Xu, Minister Jiang, and Left Guard Commander Yuan were all outstanding men of their age, loyal and steadfast in their time—some bearing stern countenance at court, some hearing of treason and refusing compliance—all cut down at the palace steps, their heads hung in the capital market.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Xu, Minister Jiang, and Left Guard Commander Yuan were the finest men of their age—some bearing stern countenance at court, some refusing treason—all cut down at the palace steps, their heads hung in the market.

sentences.zh: 宗党夷滅，豈伊一姓，禍毒所流，未知其極。

translations.literal: Clans and kindred were exterminated—not confined to a single surname; where the poison of calamity flows, its limit is not known.
translations.idiomatic: Clans and kindred were exterminated—not one family alone; where this poison flows, its limit is unknown.

sentences.zh: 昔周道告難，齊、晉勤王，漢曆中圮，虛、牟立節，異姓末屬，猶或亡軀，況幕府職同昔人，義兼臣子。

translations.literal: Formerly when the Zhou Way announced hardship, Qi and Jin labored for the king; when the Han succession collapsed midway, Xu and Mou upheld their integrity—even men of other surnames and remote stations sometimes gave their lives; how much more this headquarters, whose office matches those ancients and whose duty joins minister and son.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou faced calamity, Qi and Jin rallied to the throne; when the Han succession collapsed, Xu and Mou upheld their integrity—even men of other clans sometimes gave their lives; how much more this headquarters, whose duty joins minister and son.

sentences.zh: 所以枕戈嘗膽，苟全視息，志梟元兇，少雪仇恥。

translations.literal: Therefore we sleep upon our spears and taste gall, preserving life barely to draw breath, resolved to behead the primary villain and partly wash away our shame.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore we sleep upon our spears and taste gall, clinging to life only to draw breath, resolved to behead the primary villain and partly avenge our shame.

sentences.zh: 今命冠軍將軍領諮議中直兵柳元景、甯朔將軍領中直兵馬文恭等，統勁卒三萬，風馳徑造石頭，分趨白下；

translations.literal: Now I order Champion General and Chief of the Advisory Bureau's Central Direct Troops Liu Yuanjing, Pacifying North General and Chief of Central Direct Troops Ma Wengong, and others to command thirty thousand crack troops, galloping like the wind straight to Shitou and dividing to rush Baixia;
translations.idiomatic: I now order Champion General Liu Yuanjing, Pacifying North General Ma Wengong, and others to command thirty thousand crack troops, racing straight to Shitou and dividing toward Baixia;

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍領諮議中直兵宗愨等，勒甲楯二萬，征虜將軍領司馬武昌內史沈慶之等，領壯勇五萬，相尋就路；

translations.literal: Assistant State General and Chief of the Advisory Bureau's Central Direct Troops Zong Que and others lead twenty thousand armored shield troops; General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Chief Clerk of Wuchang Interior Minister Shen Qingzhi and others lead fifty thousand stalwart warriors, each column taking the road in succession;
translations.idiomatic: Assistant State General Zong Que leads twenty thousand armored troops; General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Shen Qingzhi leads fifty thousand stalwart warriors, each column marching in succession;

sentences.zh: 支軍別統，或焚舟破釜，步自姑孰；

translations.literal: branch armies under separate command, some burning their boats and smashing their cauldrons, march out from Gushu;
translations.idiomatic: branch armies under separate command burn their boats and smash their cauldrons, marching out from Gushu;

sentences.zh: 或迅楫蕪湖，入據雲陽。

translations.literal: others with swift oars at Wuhu enter and seize Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: others row swiftly from Wuhu to seize Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸帥，皆英果權奇，智略深贍，名震中土，勳暢遐疆。

translations.literal: All these commanders are heroic, resolute, resourceful, and extraordinary, deep in strategy and provision; their fame shakes the central lands, their merit resounds in distant borders.
translations.idiomatic: All these commanders are heroic, resourceful, and deep in strategy; their fame shakes the central lands, their merit resounds to the farthest borders.

sentences.zh: 幕府親董精悍一十余萬，授律枕戈，駱驛繼邁。

translations.literal: The headquarters personally directs more than one hundred thousand picked troops, receiving the law and sleeping upon their spears, advancing in continuous relays.
translations.idiomatic: The headquarters personally commands more than one hundred thousand picked troops, disciplined and armed, advancing in continuous relays.

sentences.zh: 司徒睿哲淵謨，赫然震發，征甲八州，電起荊郢；

translations.literal: The Minister of Education, sagely wise and profoundly scheming, rises in splendid alarm, summoning armor from eight provinces, lightning-quick from Jing and Ying;
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education, sagely and profoundly scheming, rises in splendid alarm, summoning armor from eight provinces, swift as lightning from Jing and Ying;

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍臧質忠烈協舉，雷動漢陰；

translations.literal: Champion General Zang Zhi, loyal and resolute in concerted rising, thunders in the lands west of the Han;
translations.idiomatic: Champion General Zang Zhi, loyal and resolute, thunders west of the Han;

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍硃修之誠節亮款，悉力請奮。

translations.literal: Champion General Zhu Xiuzhi, sincere in integrity and bright in loyalty, exhausts his strength in begging to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Champion General Zhu Xiuzhi, sincere and loyal, exhausts himself begging to fight.

sentences.zh: 荊、雍百萬，稍次近塗，蜀、漢之卒，續已出境。

translations.literal: A million men from Jing and Yong are drawing near along the roads; troops from Shu and Han have already crossed the borders in succession.
translations.idiomatic: A million men from Jing and Yong draw near along the roads; troops from Shu and Han have already crossed the borders.

sentences.zh: 又安東將軍誕、平西將軍遵考、前撫軍將軍蕭思話、征虜將軍魯爽、前甯朔將軍王玄謨，並密信俱到，不契同期，傳檄三吳，馳軍京邑，遠近俱發，揚旍萬里。

translations.literal: Moreover, Pacifying East General Dan, Pacifying West General Zunkao, former Pacification Army General Xiao Sihua, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Lu Shuang, and former Pacifying North General Wang Xuanmo—all sent secret letters arriving together, though not agreed on the same date—proclaiming through the Three Wu, galloping armies toward the capital; near and far all rise, banners flying for ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Pacifying East General Dan, Pacifying West General Zunkao, former Pacification Army General Xiao Sihua, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Lu Shuang, and former Pacifying North General Wang Xuanmo all sent secret letters arriving together, proclaiming through the Three Wu and galloping armies toward the capital; near and far all rise, banners flying for ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 樓艦騰川，則滄江霧咽；

translations.literal: When tower ships leap upon the rivers, the azure Yangzi chokes in mist;
translations.idiomatic: When tower ships surge upon the rivers, the azure Yangzi chokes in mist;

sentences.zh: 銳甲赴野，則林薄摧根。

translations.literal: when sharp armor rushes to the wilds, thickets and groves are uprooted at the root.
translations.idiomatic: when sharp armor rushes to the field, thickets and groves are uprooted at the root.

sentences.zh: 謀臣智士，雄夫毅卒，畜志須時，懷憤待用。

translations.literal: Counselors and wise men, heroic warriors and resolute soldiers store their resolve awaiting the hour, harboring outrage ready for use.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors and wise men, heroic warriors and resolute soldiers store their resolve for the hour, harboring outrage ready to be unleashed.

sentences.zh: 先聖靈澤，結在民心，逆順大數，冥發天理，無父之國，天下無之。

translations.literal: The late sage's numinous grace is bound in the people's hearts; the great reckoning of rebellion and obedience is secretly issued by Heaven's principle—a realm without a father, the world has never known.
translations.idiomatic: The late sage's grace lives in the people's hearts; Heaven's principle secretly ordains the reckoning of rebellion and loyalty—a realm without a father, the world has never known.

sentences.zh: 羽檄既馳，華素響會，以此眾戰，誰能抗禦，以此義動，何往不捷！

translations.literal: Once the battle proclamations have flown, the plain and the adorned answer together; with such a host for battle, who can resist? With such righteousness in motion, where will victory not come?
translations.idiomatic: Once battle proclamations fly forth, noble and common answer as one; with such a host, who can resist? With such righteousness in motion, where will we not prevail?

sentences.zh: 況逆醜無親，人鬼所背，計其同惡，不盈一旅，崇極群小，是與此周，哲人君子，必加積忌。

translations.literal: Moreover the rebel villain is without kin; men and ghosts alike turn their backs. Counting his fellow evildoers, they do not fill a single regiment; he exalts the basest rabble—this is his Zhou. Wise men and gentlemen will surely heap hatred upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the rebel is without kin; men and ghosts alike turn their backs. His fellow evildoers do not fill a single regiment; he exalts the basest rabble—this is his court. Wise men and gentlemen will surely heap hatred upon him.

sentences.zh: 傾海注螢，頹山壓卵，商、周之勢，曾何足雲。

translations.literal: Pouring the sea upon a firefly, toppling a mountain upon an egg—the forces of Shang and Zhou were scarcely worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: Pouring the sea upon a firefly, toppling a mountain upon an egg—the forces of Shang and Zhou were scarcely worth mentioning.

sentences.zh: 諸君或奕世貞賢，身囗皇渥，或勳烈肺腑，休否攸同。

translations.literal: You gentlemen are perhaps men of loyal worth for generations, your persons bathed in imperial grace; or you are men of merit in the emperor's inner circle, sharing weal and woe alike.
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen are perhaps men of loyal worth for generations, bathed in imperial grace; or men of merit in the emperor's inner circle, sharing weal and woe alike.

sentences.zh: 拘逼凶勢，俯眉寇手，含憤茹戚，不可為心。

translations.literal: Constrained by the villain's power, you bow your brows before the rebel's hand, swallowing rage and enduring grief—the heart cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Constrained by the villain's power, you bow before the rebel's hand, swallowing rage and grief the heart cannot bear.

sentences.zh: 大軍近次，威聲已接，便宜因變立功，洗雪滓累；

translations.literal: The great army is near at hand; its awesome renown already reaches you—it is fitting to seize the moment and establish merit, washing away your stains;
translations.idiomatic: The great army is near; its awesome renown already reaches you—seize the moment, establish merit, and wash away your stains;

sentences.zh: 若事有不獲，能背逆歸順，亦其次也；

translations.literal: if matters do not succeed, to turn from rebellion and return to loyalty is the next best;
translations.idiomatic: if that fails, to turn from rebellion and return to loyalty is the next best;

sentences.zh: 如有守迷遂往，黨一凶類，刑茲無赦，戮及五宗。

translations.literal: if any cling to delusion and press on, siding with the villainous crew, punishment here knows no pardon, slaughter reaching to the five kindreds.
translations.idiomatic: if any cling to delusion and side with the villains, punishment knows no pardon, slaughter reaching to the five kindreds.

sentences.zh: 賞罰之科，信如日月。

translations.literal: The standards of reward and punishment are trustworthy as sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: The standards of reward and punishment are as sure as sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 原火一燎，異物同灰，幸求多福，無貽後悔。

translations.literal: When the prairie fire blazes once, the unlike alike become ash—may you seek great blessing and leave no cause for regret.
translations.idiomatic: When the prairie fire blazes, all alike become ash—seek your blessing now and leave no cause for regret.

sentences.zh: 書到宣告，咸使聞知。

translations.literal: When this document arrives, proclaim it so that all may hear and know.
translations.idiomatic: When this document arrives, proclaim it so that all may hear and know.

sentences.zh: 劭自謂素習武事，語朝士曰：「卿等但助我理文書，勿措意戎陳。

translations.literal: Shao considered himself long practiced in military affairs and told the court gentlemen, "You need only help me manage documents—do not concern yourselves with the battle array.
translations.idiomatic: Shao considered himself a seasoned warrior and told the court, "You need only help me with documents—leave military affairs to me.

sentences.zh: 若有寇難，吾當自出，唯恐賊虜不敢動爾。」

translations.literal: If bandits come, I shall go out myself—I only fear the rebel barbarians will not dare stir."
translations.idiomatic: If enemies come, I shall go out myself—I only fear the rebels will not dare stir."

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉殷沖掌綜文符，左衛將軍尹弘配衣軍旅，蕭斌總眾事，中外戒嚴。

translations.literal: Director of Retainers Yin Chong managed all documents and tallies; Left Guard General Yin Hong coordinated military dress and troops; Xiao Bin oversaw all affairs; inside and outside the palace were placed under martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Retainers Yin Chong managed all documents; Left Guard General Yin Hong coordinated the troops; Xiao Bin oversaw all affairs; martial law was declared throughout the palace and capital.

sentences.zh: 防守世祖子於侍中下省，南譙王義宣諸子於太倉空屋。

translations.literal: The heir apparent's sons were guarded in the lower bureau of the Attendants-in-Ordinary; the sons of Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan were held in empty rooms of the Great Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent's sons were confined in the attendants' lower bureau; Yixuan's sons were held in empty rooms of the Great Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 劭使浚與世祖書曰：「聞弟忽起狂檄，阻兵反噬，縉紳憤歎，義夫激怒。

translations.literal: Shao had Jun write to the heir apparent: "I hear that you, younger brother, have suddenly raised a mad proclamation, blocking the army and turning to devour your kin—the gentry are indignant and sighing, men of righteousness are roused to anger.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had Jun write to the heir apparent: "I hear you have suddenly raised a mad proclamation, blocking the army and turning on your kin—the gentry are indignant, men of righteousness are roused to anger.

sentences.zh: 古來陵上內侮，誰不夷滅，弟洞覽墳籍，豈不斯具。

translations.literal: From antiquity onward, those who insulted their superiors and brought internal strife—who was not exterminated? Younger brother, you have thoroughly perused the tombs and records—is this not fully set forth there?
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity onward, those who insulted their superiors and brought internal strife—who was not exterminated? You have read the classics—is this not fully set forth there?

sentences.zh: 今主上天縱英聖，靈武宏發，自登宸極，威澤兼宣，人懷甘死之志，物競舍生之節。

translations.literal: Now our lord above is Heaven-endowed, heroic and sage; his numinous martial power flourishes grandly; since ascending the imperial pinnacle, authority and grace are both proclaimed—men harbor the will to die gladly for him, all things compete in the integrity of giving their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord is Heaven-endowed, heroic and sage; his martial power flourishes; since ascending the throne, authority and grace are both proclaimed—men gladly die for him, all things compete in giving their lives.

sentences.zh: 弟蒙眷遇，著自少長，東宮之歡，其來如昨，而信惑奸邪，忘茲恩友，此之不義，人鬼同疾。

translations.literal: Younger brother, you have enjoyed favor from childhood to maturity; the joys of the Eastern Palace are as yesterday—yet you believed and were deluded by wicked men, forgetting this grace and friendship; such unrighteousness, men and ghosts alike abhor.
translations.idiomatic: You have enjoyed favor from childhood; the joys of the Eastern Palace are as yesterday—yet you believed wicked men and forgot this grace; such unrighteousness, men and ghosts alike abhor.

sentences.zh: 今水步諸軍悉已備辦，上親禦六師，太保又乘鉞臨統，吾與烏羊，相尋即道。

translations.literal: Now the river and land forces are all prepared; the emperor will personally lead the Six Armies; the Grand Tutor again bears the battle-axe and commands in person; I and the Black Sheep will take the road in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The river and land forces are all prepared; the emperor will personally lead the Six Armies; the Grand Tutor again bears the battle-axe; I and the Black Sheep will march in succession.

sentences.zh: 所以淹霆緩電者，猶冀弟迷而知返爾。

translations.literal: The reason we delay the thunderbolt and slow the lightning is still to hope that you, younger brother, lost though you are, may yet know to return.
translations.idiomatic: We delay the thunderbolt only in hope that you, though lost, may yet know to return.

sentences.zh: 故略示懷，言不盡意，主上聖恩，每厚法師，今在殿內住，想弟欲知消息，故及。」

translations.literal: Therefore I briefly show my feelings—words cannot exhaust my meaning. The lord above's sagely grace is always generous to Fashi; he now dwells within the hall. I thought younger brother would wish to know news of him, and so I mention this."
translations.idiomatic: I briefly show my feelings—words cannot exhaust my meaning. The emperor's grace is always generous to Fashi; he now dwells within the hall. I thought you would wish to know, and so I mention this."

sentences.zh: 烏羊者，南平王鑠；

translations.literal: Black Sheep" was Prince of Nanping Shuo;
translations.idiomatic: Black Sheep" referred to Shuo, Prince of Nanping;

sentences.zh: 法師，世祖世子小名也。

translations.literal: Fashi was the childhood name of the heir apparent's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Fashi was the childhood name of the heir apparent's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 劭欲殺三鎮士庶家口，江夏王義恭、何尚之說之曰：「凡舉大事者，不顧家口。

translations.literal: Shao wished to kill the families of the gentry and commoners of the three commanderies. Prince of Jiangxia Yigong and He Shangzhi admonished him, saying, "All who undertake great affairs disregard family dependents.
translations.idiomatic: Shao wished to kill the families of those in the three commanderies. Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, and He Shangzhi admonished him: "All who undertake great affairs disregard family dependents.

sentences.zh: 且多是驅逼，今忽誅其餘累，正足堅彼意耳。」

translations.literal: Moreover most were driven and compelled; if you now suddenly execute their remaining dependents, you will only harden their resolve."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover most were coerced; if you now execute their families, you will only harden their resolve."

sentences.zh: 劭謂為然，乃下書一無所問。

translations.literal: Shao thought this correct and therefore issued an edict that nothing was to be investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Shao agreed and issued an edict that no inquiries were to be made.

sentences.zh: 使褚湛之戍石頭，劉思考鎮東府。

translations.literal: He sent Chu Chenzhi to garrison Shitou and Liu Sikao to guard the Eastern Palace headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chu Chenzhi to garrison Shitou and Liu Sikao to guard the Eastern Palace headquarters.

sentences.zh: 浚及蕭斌勸劭勒水軍自上決戰，若不爾，則保據梁山。

translations.literal: Jun and Xiao Bin urged Shao to muster the river forces and fight a decisive battle upstream; if not, then to hold and defend Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Xiao Bin urged Shao to muster the river fleet for a decisive battle upstream, or else hold Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭慮義兵倉卒，船舫陋小，不宜水戰。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiangxia Yigong feared the righteous army had been raised in haste, their boats crude and small, ill-suited for river combat.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, feared the righteous army had been raised in haste with crude, small boats ill-suited for river combat.

sentences.zh: 乃進策曰：「賊駿少年未習軍旅，遠來疲弊，宜以逸待之。

translations.literal: He therefore submitted a stratagem: "The rebel Jun is young and unpracticed in military affairs; coming from afar he is weary and spent—you should await him at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a stratagem: "The rebel Jun is young and inexperienced; coming from afar he is weary—you should await him at ease.

sentences.zh: 今遠出梁山，則京都空弱，東軍乘虛，容能為患。

translations.literal: If you now go far out to Liangshan, the capital will be empty and weak; the eastern army may seize the opening and could become a threat.
translations.idiomatic: If you march far to Liangshan, the capital will be left weak; the eastern army may seize the opening and become a threat.

sentences.zh: 若分力兩赴，則兵散勢離。

translations.literal: If you divide your strength and go in two directions, the army will scatter and momentum will dissolve.
translations.idiomatic: If you divide your forces in two directions, the army will scatter and momentum will dissolve.

sentences.zh: 不如養銳待期，坐而勸釁。」

translations.literal: It would be better to nurture sharpness and await the appointed time, sitting still and encouraging provocation."
translations.idiomatic: Better to nurture our strength and await the moment, sitting still and letting them provoke themselves."

sentences.zh: 劭善其議，蕭斌厲色曰：「南中郎二十年少，業能建如此大事，豈複可量。

translations.literal: Shao approved this counsel. Xiao Bin said sternly, "The Southern Gentlemen-in-Attendance is only twenty years old, yet he has already accomplished such a great affair—how can he still be measured?
translations.idiomatic: Shao approved this plan. Xiao Bin said sternly, "The Southern Gentlemen-in-Attendance is only twenty, yet he has already accomplished so much—who can gauge his capacity?

sentences.zh: 三方同惡，勢據上流，沈慶之甚練軍事，柳元景、宗愨屢嘗立功。

translations.literal: Three regions share the same evil; they hold the upper reaches in strength. Shen Qingzhi is deeply practiced in military affairs; Liu Yuanjing and Zong Que have repeatedly won merit.
translations.idiomatic: Three regions share their rebellion and hold the upper Yangzi; Shen Qingzhi is a seasoned commander, and Liu Yuanjing and Zong Que have won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 形勢如此，實非小敵。

translations.literal: The situation being thus, they are truly no small enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In such a situation they are no small enemy.

sentences.zh: 唯宜及人情未離，尚可決力一戰。

translations.literal: We should only strike while popular sentiment has not yet departed from us—we may still stake everything on one battle.
translations.idiomatic: We should strike while loyalty still holds and stake everything on one decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 端坐台城，何由得久。

translations.literal: Sitting idle in Terrace City, how can we last long?
translations.idiomatic: Sitting idle in Terrace City, how can we endure?

sentences.zh: 主相咸無戰意，此自天也。」

translations.literal: The lord and the chief minister alike lack fighting spirit—this is Heaven's doing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and chief minister alike lack fighting spirit—this is Heaven's will."

sentences.zh: 劭不納。

translations.literal: Shao would not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: Shao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 疑朝廷舊臣悉不為己用，厚接王羅漢、魯秀，悉以兵事委之，多賜珍玩美色，以悅其意。

translations.literal: Suspecting that the old ministers of the court would none of them serve him, he treated Wang Luohan and Lu Xiu generously, entrusting all military affairs to them and bestowing many precious objects and beautiful women to please them.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting the court's veteran ministers would not serve him, he lavished favor on Wang Luohan and Lu Xiu, entrusting all military affairs to them and bestowing treasures and beautiful women to win them over.

sentences.zh: 羅漢先為南平王鑠右軍參軍，劭以其有將用，故以心膂委焉。

translations.literal: Luohan had earlier been a staff officer of the Right Army under Prince of Nanping Shuo; Shao, because he had general's talent, therefore entrusted him as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Luohan had served as a staff officer under Shuo, Prince of Nanping; Shao valued his military talent and entrusted him as a close confidant.

sentences.zh: 或勸劭保石頭城者，劭曰：「昔人所以固石頭，俟諸侯勤王爾。
