translations.literal: When some urged Shao to hold Shitou fortress, Shao said, "Men of old fortified Shitou in order to await the feudal lords coming to aid the king.
translations.idiomatic: When some urged him to hold Shitou fortress, Shao said, "Men of old fortified Shitou to await the lords coming to aid the throne.

sentences.zh: 我若守此，誰當見救。

translations.literal: If I hold this place, who will come to rescue me?
translations.idiomatic: If I hold this place, who will rescue me?

sentences.zh: 唯應力戰決之，不然不克。」

translations.literal: We should only fight with full strength to decide the matter; otherwise we cannot prevail."
translations.idiomatic: We must fight with full strength to decide the matter; otherwise we cannot prevail."

sentences.zh: 日日自出行軍，慰勞將士，親督都水治船艦，焚南岸，驅百姓家悉渡水北。

translations.literal: Every day he went out in person to review the army, comfort and reward the troops, personally oversee the Directorate of Waterways in repairing ships, burn the south bank, and drive all common households to cross to the north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he went out to review the troops, comfort the soldiers, personally oversee shipbuilding, burn the south bank, and drive all civilians across to the north bank.

sentences.zh: 使有司奏立子偉之為皇太子，以褚湛之為後將軍、丹陽尹，置佐史，驃騎將軍始興王浚為侍中、中書監、司徒、錄尚書六條事，中軍將軍南平王鑠為使持節、都督南兗兗青徐冀五州諸軍事、征北將軍、開府儀同三司、南兗州刺史，新除左將軍、丹陽尹建平王宏為散騎常侍、鎮軍將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: He had the relevant offices memorialize to install his son Weizhi as crown prince; Chu Chenzhi was made Rear General and Intendant of Danyang with staff officers appointed; Rapid Cavalry General Prince of Shixing Jun was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Minister of Education, and Recorder of the Six Articles of the Masters of Writing; Central Army General Prince of Nanping Shuo was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs of the five provinces of southern Yan, Yan, Qing, Xu, and Ji, General Who Campaigns North, with office equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of southern Yan; the newly appointed Left General and Intendant of Danyang Prince of Jianping Hong was made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Pacification Army General, and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had officials memorialize to install his son Weizhi as crown prince; Chu Chenzhi was made Rear General and intendant of Danyang; Jun, Prince of Shixing and Rapid Cavalry General, was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Minister of Education, and recorder of the six articles; Shuo, Prince of Nanping and Central Army General, was made commander of five provinces with the title General Who Campaigns North; and Hong, Prince of Jianping, was made Pacification Army General and inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 龐秀之自石頭先眾南奔，人情由是大震。

translations.literal: Pang Xiuzhi fled south from Shitou ahead of the masses, and popular sentiment was thereby greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xiuzhi fled south from Shitou ahead of the troops, and morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 以征虜將軍營道侯義綦即本號為湘州刺史，輔國將軍檀和之為西中郎將、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Marquis of Yingdao Yiqi was given his original title as Inspector of Xiangzhou; Assistant State General Tan Hezhi was made Western Gentlemen-in-Attendance and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqi, Marquis of Yingdao and General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, was made inspector of Xiangzhou; Tan Hezhi, Assistant State General, was made Western Gentlemen-in-Attendance and inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 十九日，義軍至新林，劭登石頭烽火樓望之。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day the righteous army reached Xinlin; Shao ascended the beacon tower at Shitou to watch them.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth the righteous army reached Xinlin; Shao climbed the beacon tower at Shitou to watch them.

sentences.zh: 二十一日，義軍至新亭。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day the righteous army reached Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first the righteous army reached Xinting.

sentences.zh: 時魯秀屯白石，劭召秀與王羅漢共屯硃雀門。

translations.literal: At that time Lu Xiu was encamped at Baishi; Shao summoned Xiu and Wang Luohan to encamp together at the Vermilion Sparrow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiu was then encamped at Baishi; Shao summoned him and Wang Luohan to hold the Vermilion Sparrow Gate together.

sentences.zh: 蕭斌統步軍，褚湛之統水軍。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin commanded the infantry; Chu Chenzhi commanded the river forces.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin commanded the infantry; Chu Chenzhi commanded the river fleet.

sentences.zh: 二十二日，使蕭斌率魯秀、王羅漢等精兵萬人攻新亭壘，劭登硃雀門躬自督率，將士懷劭重賞，皆為之力戰。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day he had Xiao Bin lead Lu Xiu, Wang Luohan, and other picked troops numbering ten thousand to attack the Xinting fort; Shao ascended the Vermilion Sparrow Gate and personally directed them. The officers and soldiers, cherishing Shao's heavy rewards, all fought with full strength for him.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second Xiao Bin led ten thousand picked troops under Lu Xiu and Wang Luohan against the Xinting fort while Shao personally directed from the Vermilion Sparrow Gate. His officers and soldiers, tempted by heavy rewards, fought with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 將克，而秀斂軍遽止，為柳元景等所乘，故大敗。

translations.literal: They were about to prevail when Xiu suddenly halted and withdrew his army; Liu Yuanjing and others seized the opening, and so they were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They were on the verge of victory when Xiu suddenly halted his troops; Liu Yuanjing and others seized the opening and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 劭又率腹心同惡自來攻壘，元景複破之；

translations.literal: Shao again led his trusted fellow evildoers in person to attack the fort, and Yuanjing once more defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: Shao again led his trusted conspirators in person to attack the fort, and Yuanjing defeated them once more;

sentences.zh: 劭走還硃雀門，蕭斌臂為流矢所中。

translations.literal: Shao fled back to the Vermilion Sparrow Gate; Xiao Bin's arm was struck by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Shao fled back to the Vermilion Sparrow Gate; a stray arrow struck Xiao Bin's arm.

sentences.zh: 褚湛之攜二子與檀和之同共歸順。

translations.literal: Chu Chenzhi took his two sons and together with Tan Hezhi submitted in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Chenzhi took his two sons and submitted together with Tan Hezhi.

sentences.zh: 劭駭懼，走還台城。

translations.literal: Shao, terrified, fled back to Terrace City.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Shao fled back to Terrace City.

sentences.zh: 其夜，魯秀又南奔。

translations.literal: That night Lu Xiu fled south again.
translations.idiomatic: That night Lu Xiu fled south again.

sentences.zh: 時江夏王義恭謀據石頭，會劭已令浚及蕭斌備守。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Jiangxia Yigong plotted to seize Shitou, but Shao had already ordered Jun and Xiao Bin to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, plotted to seize Shitou, but Shao had already ordered Jun and Xiao Bin to guard it.

sentences.zh: 劭並焚京都軍籍，置立郡縣，悉屬司隸為民。

translations.literal: Shao also burned the capital's military registers, established commanderies and counties, and made all belong to the Director of Retainers as common households.
translations.idiomatic: Shao also burned the capital's military registers, established commanderies and counties, and registered all as common households under the Director of Retainers.

sentences.zh: 以前軍將軍、輔國將軍王羅漢為左衛將軍，輔國如故，左軍王正見為太子左衛率。

translations.literal: Former Forward Army General and Assistant State General Wang Luohan was made Left Guard General, retaining Assistant State General as before; Left Army Wang Zhengjian was made Crown Prince's Left Guard Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Luohan was made Left Guard General while retaining his Assistant State General title; Wang Zhengjian was made the crown prince's Left Guard Commander.

sentences.zh: 二十五日，義恭單馬南奔，自東掖門出，於冶渚過淮。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day Yigong fled south alone on horseback, exiting through the Eastern Corner Gate and crossing the Huai at Yezhu.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth Yigong fled south alone on horseback, exiting through the Eastern Corner Gate and crossing the Huai at Yezhu.

sentences.zh: 東掖門隊主吳道興是臧質門人，冶渚軍主原稚孫是世祖故史，義恭得免。

translations.literal: The squad leader at the Eastern Corner Gate, Wu Daoxing, was a client of Zang Zhi; the garrison commander at Yezhu, Yuan Zhisun, was a former clerk of the heir apparent—thus Yigong escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Daoxing, squad leader at the Eastern Corner Gate, was a client of Zang Zhi; Yuan Zhisun, garrison commander at Yezhu, was a former clerk of the heir apparent—thus Yigong escaped.

sentences.zh: 劭遣騎追討，騎至冶渚，義恭始得渡淮。

translations.literal: Shao sent cavalry in pursuit; the riders reached Yezhu only after Yigong had just crossed the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent cavalry in pursuit; they reached Yezhu only after Yigong had crossed the Huai.

sentences.zh: 義恭佐史義故二千余人，隨從南奔，多為追兵所殺。

translations.literal: More than two thousand of Yigong's staff officers and old retainers followed him south in flight; most were killed by the pursuing troops.
translations.idiomatic: More than two thousand of Yigong's staff and retainers followed him south; most were killed by pursuers.

sentences.zh: 遣浚殺義恭諸子。

translations.literal: He sent Jun to kill Yigong's sons.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Jun to kill Yigong's sons.

sentences.zh: 以輦迎蔣侯神像于宮內，啟顙乞恩，拜為大司馬，封鐘山郡王，食邑萬戶，加節鉞。

translations.literal: He had the spirit image of Lord Jiang brought into the palace by imperial carriage, bowed his forehead begging grace, and enfeoffed him as Grand Marshal, Prince of Zhongshan commandery, with a fief of ten thousand households and the battle-axe of authority.
translations.idiomatic: He had the spirit image of Lord Jiang brought into the palace by imperial carriage, bowed begging grace, and enfeoffed him as Grand Marshal, Prince of Zhongshan, with ten thousand households and the battle-axe of authority.

sentences.zh: 蘇侯為驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Lord Su was made Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Su was made Rapid Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 使南平王鑠為祝文，罪狀世祖。

translations.literal: He had Prince of Nanping Shuo compose the prayer text enumerating the heir apparent's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He had Shuo, Prince of Nanping, compose the prayer text enumerating the heir apparent's crimes.

sentences.zh: 加浚使持節、都督南徐會二州諸軍事、領太子太傅、南徐州刺史，給班劍二十人；

translations.literal: Jun was further given the Staff, command over military affairs of the two provinces of southern Xu and Hui, appointment as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince and Inspector of southern Xu, and twenty ceremonial swords;
translations.idiomatic: Jun was given the Staff, command over southern Xu and Hui, appointment as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince and inspector of southern Xu, and twenty ceremonial swords;

sentences.zh: 征北將軍、南兗州刺史南平王鑠進號驃騎將軍，與浚並錄尚書事。

translations.literal: General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of southern Yan Prince of Nanping Shuo was advanced to Rapid Cavalry General and, with Jun, recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo, Prince of Nanping, General Who Campaigns North and inspector of southern Yan, was promoted to Rapid Cavalry General and, with Jun, recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 二十七日，臨軒拜息偉之為太子，百官皆戎服，劭獨袞衣。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day, facing the hall, he invested his son Weizhi as crown prince; all officials wore military dress, Shao alone wore imperial robes.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh he invested his son Weizhi as crown prince before the hall; all officials wore armor while Shao alone wore imperial robes.

sentences.zh: 下書大赦天下，唯世祖、劉義恭、義宣、誕不在原例，餘黨一無所問。

translations.literal: He issued an edict granting a great amnesty throughout the realm; only the heir apparent, Liu Yigong, Yixuan, and Dan were excluded from the general rule—the rest of the faction were not questioned at all.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a great amnesty; only the heir apparent, Yigong, Yixuan, and Dan were excluded—the rest of the faction went unquestioned.

sentences.zh: 先遣太保參軍庾道、員外散騎侍郎硃和之，又遣殿中將軍燕欽東拒誕。

translations.literal: He first sent Grand Tutor staff officer Yu Dao and Extraordinary Attendant-Cadet of Scattered Cavalry Zhu Hezhi; he also sent Palace General Yan Qin east to resist Dan.
translations.idiomatic: He first sent Grand Tutor staff officer Yu Dao and extraordinary Attendant-Cadet Zhu Hezhi, and also sent Palace General Yan Qin east to resist Dan.

sentences.zh: 五月，世祖所遣參軍顧彬之及誕前軍，並至曲阿，與道相遇，與戰，大破之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the staff officer Gu Binzhi sent by the heir apparent and Dan's vanguard both reached Qu'e, met Dao, fought, and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Gu Binzhi, staff officer of the heir apparent, and Dan's vanguard reached Qu'e, met Dao in battle, and routed him utterly.

sentences.zh: 劭遣人焚燒都水西裝及左尚方，決破柏崗方山埭以絕東軍。

translations.literal: Shao sent men to burn the western workshops of the Directorate of Waterways and the Left Palace Workshops, and breached the Baigang and Fangshan dams to cut off the eastern army.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent men to burn the western workshops of the Directorate of Waterways and the Left Palace Workshops, and breached the Baigang and Fangshan dams to block the eastern army.

sentences.zh: 又悉以上守家之丁巷居者，緣淮豎舶船為樓，多設大弩。

translations.literal: He also took all adult males from households guarding the walls and those dwelling in alleys, erected barge-ships along the river as towers, and set up many large crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: He also conscripted all adult males from wall-guard households and alley dwellers, erected barge-towers along the river, and set up many large crossbows.

sentences.zh: 又使司隸治中監琅邪郡事羊希柵斷班瀆、白石諸水口。

translations.literal: He also had the Director of Retainers' supervising administrator for Langye commandery affairs, Yang Xi, barricade the mouths of the Banyu, Baishi, and other waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yang Xi, supervising administrator of Langye under the Director of Retainers, barricade the mouths of the Banyu, Baishi, and other waterways.

sentences.zh: 于時男丁既盡，召婦女親役。

translations.literal: By then adult males were exhausted, and women were summoned for labor in person.
translations.idiomatic: By then adult males were exhausted, and women were summoned for labor.

sentences.zh: 其月三日，魯秀等募勇士五百人攻大航，鉤得一舶。

translations.literal: On the third day of that month Lu Xiu and others recruited five hundred brave men to attack the Great Crossing and hooked one barge.
translations.idiomatic: On the third of that month Lu Xiu recruited five hundred men to attack the Great Crossing and seized one barge.

sentences.zh: 王羅漢副楊恃德命使複航，羅漢昏酣作伎，聞官軍已渡，驚懼放仗歸降。

translations.literal: Wang Luohan's deputy Yang Side ordered the messenger to restore navigation; Luohan, drunk and drowsy amid entertainments, heard the government army had crossed, and in shock and fear cast aside his weapons and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Luohan's deputy Yang Side ordered navigation restored; Luohan, drunk amid entertainments, heard the government army had crossed, cast aside his weapons, and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 緣渚幢隊，以次奔散，器仗鼓蓋，充塞街衢。

translations.literal: The banner squads along the shore fled in succession; weapons, drums, and canopies filled the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Banner squads along the shore fled in succession; weapons, drums, and canopies filled the streets.

sentences.zh: 是夜，劭閉守六門，於門內鑿塹立柵，以露車為樓，城內沸亂，無複綱紀。

translations.literal: That night Shao closed and guarded the six gates, dug moats and erected palisades inside the gates, used open wagons as towers—the city seethed in chaos and order was no more.
translations.idiomatic: That night Shao sealed the six gates, dug moats and erected palisades inside them, and used open wagons as towers—the city seethed in chaos and all order collapsed.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹尹弘、前軍將軍孟宗嗣等下及將吏，並逾城出奔。

translations.literal: Intendant of Danyang Yin Hong, Forward Army General Meng Zongsi, and others below them among officers and clerks all climbed over the wall and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hong, intendant of Danyang, Forward Army General Meng Zongsi, and officers and clerks below them all climbed over the wall and fled.

sentences.zh: 劭使詹叔兒燒輦及袞冕服。

translations.literal: Shao had Zhan Shuer burn the imperial carriages and the robes and caps of state.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had Zhan Shuer burn the imperial carriages and the robes and caps of state.

sentences.zh: 蕭斌聞大航不守，惶窘不知所為，宣令所統，皆使解甲，自石頭遣息約詣闕請罪，尋戴白幡來降，即於軍門伏誅。

translations.literal: When Xiao Bin heard the Great Crossing could not be held, he was panicked and at a loss; he proclaimed to those he commanded that all should lay down armor; from Shitou he sent his son Yue to the palace to beg forgiveness, then soon came wearing a white banner to surrender and was immediately executed at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Bin heard the Great Crossing had fallen, he panicked, ordered his troops to lay down their arms, sent his son Yue from Shitou to beg forgiveness, then came wearing a white banner to surrender and was executed at the army gate.

sentences.zh: 四日，太尉江夏王義恭登硃雀門，總群帥，遣魯秀、薛安都、程天祚等直趣宣陽門。

translations.literal: On the fourth day Grand Commandant Prince of Jiangxia Yigong ascended the Vermilion Sparrow Gate, took overall command of the commanders, and sent Lu Xiu, Xue Andu, Cheng Tianzuo, and others straight toward the Xuanyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth Grand Commandant Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, ascended the Vermilion Sparrow Gate, took command of the generals, and sent Lu Xiu, Xue Andu, Cheng Tianzuo, and others straight to the Xuanyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 劭軍主徐興祖、羅訓、虞丘要兒等率眾來降。

translations.literal: Shao's commanders Xu Xingzu, Luo Xun, Yuqiu Yaor, and others led their forces to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's commanders Xu Xingzu, Luo Xun, Yuqiu Yaor, and others led their forces to surrender.

sentences.zh: 劭先遣龍驤將軍陳叔兒東討，事急，召還。

translations.literal: Shao had earlier sent Dragon-Prancing General Chen Shuer on an eastern campaign; when matters grew urgent he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had earlier sent Dragon-Prancing General Chen Shuer east; when matters grew urgent he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 是日，始入建陽門，遙見官軍，所領並棄仗走。

translations.literal: That day he had just entered the Jianyang Gate when, seeing the government army from afar, all those he led cast aside their weapons and fled.
translations.idiomatic: That day he had just entered the Jianyang Gate when, seeing the government army in the distance, all his men cast aside their weapons and fled.

sentences.zh: 劭腹心白直同諸逆先屯閶闔門外，並走還入殿。

translations.literal: Shao's trusted white-uniform direct guards and the other rebels who had first encamped outside the Changhe Gate all ran back into the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's trusted white-uniform guards and other rebels encamped outside the Changhe Gate all ran back into the palace.

sentences.zh: 天祚與安都副譚金因而乘之，即得俱入。

translations.literal: Tianzuo and Andu's deputy Tan Jin seized the moment and were able to enter together at once.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo and Andu's deputy Tan Jin seized the moment and entered together.

sentences.zh: 安都及軍主武念、宋越等相繼進，臧質大軍從廣莫門入，同會太極殿前，即斬太子左衛率王正見。

translations.literal: Andu and army commanders Wu Nian, Song Yue, and others advanced in succession; Zang Zhi's great army entered through the Guangmo Gate; all met before the Supreme Ultimate Hall and immediately beheaded Crown Prince's Left Guard Commander Wang Zhengjian.
translations.idiomatic: Andu and commanders Wu Nian and Song Yue advanced in succession; Zang Zhi's great army entered through the Guangmo Gate; all met before the Supreme Ultimate Hall and beheaded Wang Zhengjian, the crown prince's Left Guard Commander.

sentences.zh: 建平、東海等七王並號哭俱出。

translations.literal: The seven princes of Jianping, Donghai, and the others all came out together wailing.
translations.idiomatic: The seven princes of Jianping, Donghai, and others all came out together wailing.

sentences.zh: 劭穿西垣入武庫井中，隊副高禽執之。

translations.literal: Shao broke through the western wall and entered the well of the armory; squad deputy Gao Qin seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao broke through the western wall and hid in the armory well; squad deputy Gao Qin seized him.

sentences.zh: 浚率左右數十人，與南平王鑠於西明門出，俱共南奔。

translations.literal: Jun led several dozen attendants and, with Prince of Nanping Shuo, went out through the Western Bright Gate and fled south together.
translations.idiomatic: Jun led several dozen attendants and, with Shuo, Prince of Nanping, fled south through the Western Bright Gate.

sentences.zh: 于越城遇江夏王義恭，浚下馬曰：「南中郎今何所作？」

translations.literal: At Yuecheng Jun met Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, dismounted, and said, "What is the Southern Gentlemen-in-Attendance doing now?"
translations.idiomatic: At Yuecheng Jun met Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, dismounted, and asked, "What is the Southern Gentlemen-in-Attendance doing now?"

sentences.zh: 義恭曰：「四海無統，百司固請，上已俯順群心，君臨萬國。」

translations.literal: Yigong said, "The four seas lack a ruler; the hundred offices firmly petitioned; the lord above has bowed to the people's hearts and rules the ten thousand states."
translations.idiomatic: Yigong replied, "The realm lacks a ruler; the hundred offices petitioned; the emperor has bowed to the people's will and rules the realm."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「虎頭來得無晚乎？」

translations.literal: He also said, "Has Tiger Head come not too late?"
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Has Tiger Head come too late?"

sentences.zh: 義恭曰：「殊當恨晚。」

translations.literal: Yigong said, "Indeed one should deeply regret the lateness."
translations.idiomatic: Yigong said, "Indeed—it is far too late."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「故當不死耶？」

translations.literal: He also said, "So I suppose I shall not die after all?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun asked, "So I am not to die after all?"

sentences.zh: 義恭曰：「可詣行闕請罪。」

translations.literal: Yigong said, "You may go to the traveling palace gate and beg forgiveness."
translations.idiomatic: Yigong said, "You may go to the traveling palace and beg forgiveness."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「未審猶能賜一職自效不？」

translations.literal: He also said, "I wonder whether I might still be granted a post to offer my service?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun asked, "Might I still be granted a post to serve?"

sentences.zh: 義恭又曰：「此未可量。」

translations.literal: Yigong again said, "That cannot yet be measured."
translations.idiomatic: Yigong replied, "That cannot yet be known."

sentences.zh: 勒與俱歸，於道斬首。

translations.literal: He was compelled to return with him and was beheaded on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was compelled to return with him and was beheaded on the road.

sentences.zh: 浚字休明，將產之夕，有鵩鳥鳴於屋上。

translations.literal: Jun, style name Xiuming, on the night he was to be born a owl-falcon cried upon the roof.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, styled Xiuming, on the night before his birth an owl-falcon cried upon the roof.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十三年，年八歲，封始興王。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanjia, at age eight, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yuanjia, at eight he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 十六年，都督湘州諸軍事、後將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was made Commander over military affairs of Xiangzhou, Rear General, and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made commander of Xiangzhou military affairs, Rear General, and inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 仍遷使持節、都督南豫豫司雍並五州諸軍事、南豫州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was then transferred as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs of the five provinces of southern Yu, Yu, Si, Yong, and Bing, and Inspector of southern Yu, his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Bearer of the Staff, commander of five provinces including southern Yu, Yu, Si, Yong, and Bing, and inspector of southern Yu, retaining his generalship.

sentences.zh: 十七年，為揚州刺史，將軍如故，置佐領兵。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he became Inspector of Yangzhou, his generalship unchanged, with staff officers appointed to lead troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he became inspector of Yangzhou, retaining his generalship, with staff officers appointed to lead troops.

sentences.zh: 十九年，罷府。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year his headquarters was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year his headquarters was abolished.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，加散騎常侍，進號中軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was given Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and advanced to Central Army General.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was given Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and promoted to Central Army General.

sentences.zh: 明年，浚上言：「所統吳興郡，衿帶重山，地多汙澤，泉流歸集，疏決遲壅，時雨未過，已至漂沒。

translations.literal: The following year Jun memorialized: "The Wuxing commandery under my command is girdled by heavy mountains and has many marshes; streams converge and drainage is slow and blocked—before the seasonal rains have passed, flooding already occurs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Jun memorialized: "Wuxing commandery under my command is girdled by mountains and has many marshes; streams converge and drainage is slow—before the rains have passed, flooding already occurs.

sentences.zh: 或方春輟耕，或開秋沈稼，田家徒苦，防遏無方。

translations.literal: Sometimes plowing is halted in spring, sometimes crops sink in the opening autumn—the farming households suffer in vain, with no means to prevent or block it.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes spring plowing is halted, sometimes autumn crops are drowned—farmers suffer in vain with no means to prevent it.

sentences.zh: 彼邦奧區，地沃民阜，一歲稱稔，則穰被京城；

translations.literal: That region is a fertile heartland, its land rich and its people abundant; one good harvest spreads abundance to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: That region is a fertile heartland; one good harvest feeds the capital;

sentences.zh: 時或水潦，由數郡為災。

translations.literal: when floods come, several commanderies suffer disaster together.
translations.idiomatic: when floods come, several commanderies suffer together.

sentences.zh: 頃年以來，儉多豐寡，雖賑賚周給，傾耗國儲，公私之弊，方在未已。

translations.literal: In recent years lean years have outnumbered abundant ones; though relief and grants are distributed widely, the state stores are drained—the harm to public and private interests is still not ended.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years lean years have outnumbered abundant ones; though relief is distributed widely, state stores are drained—the harm to public and private interests continues.

sentences.zh: 州民姚嶠比通便宜，以為二吳、晉陵、義興四郡，同注太湖，而松江滬瀆壅噎不利，故處處湧溢，浸漬成災。

translations.literal: A commandery resident named Yao Qiao, versed in practical measures, held that the four commanderies of the Two Wu, Jinling, and Yixing all drain into Lake Tai, while the Song River and Hudu are choked and impeded, so water overflows everywhere and soaking becomes disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Qiao, a commandery resident versed in practical measures, held that the four commanderies of the Two Wu, Jinling, and Yixing all drain into Lake Tai, while the Song River and Hudu are choked, so water overflows everywhere into disaster.

sentences.zh: 欲從武康珝溪開漕穀湖，直出海口，一百餘裏，穿渠浛必無閡滯。

translations.literal: He wished to open a canal from Wukang's Xu Brook through the Grain Transport Lake straight to the sea mouth, more than one hundred li—once the channel is cut through there will certainly be no obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed opening a canal from Wukang's Xu Brook through the Grain Transport Lake straight to the sea, more than one hundred li—once cut through there would be no obstruction.

sentences.zh: 自去踐行量度，二十許載。

translations.literal: Since going in person to measure and survey, about twenty years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: He had been measuring and surveying in person for about twenty years.

sentences.zh: 去十一年大水，已詣前刺史臣義康欲陳此計，即遣主簿盛曇泰隨嶠周行，互生疑難，議遂寢息。

translations.literal: Eleven years ago, in a great flood, he had already gone to the former inspector, your subject Yikang, wishing to present this plan; he immediately sent chief clerk Sheng Tantai to follow Qiao on a circuit tour, but mutual doubts arose and the proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven years ago, in a great flood, he had already approached former inspector Yikang with this plan; Yikang sent chief clerk Sheng Tantai to tour with Qiao, but mutual doubts arose and the proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 既事關大利，宜加研盡，登遣議曹從事史虞長孫與吳興太守孔山士同共履行，准望地勢，格評高下，其川源由曆，莫不踐校，圖畫形便，詳加算考，如所較量，決謂可立。

translations.literal: Since the matter concerns great benefit, it should be studied exhaustively. I have sent Review Bureau staff officer Yu Changsun together with Administrator of Wuxing Kong Shanshi to conduct the route, gauge terrain, and evaluate heights; every watercourse has been traced and verified, maps drawn of the terrain, and calculations made in detail—by the comparison, it is decisively judged feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Since the matter concerns great benefit, it should be studied exhaustively. I sent Review Bureau staff officer Yu Changsun with Wuxing administrator Kong Shanshi to survey the route, gauge terrain, and verify every watercourse—by detailed calculation, it is judged feasible.

sentences.zh: 尋四郡同患，非獨吳興，若此浛獲通，列邦蒙益。

translations.literal: Soon all four commanderies share the same affliction—not Wuxing alone; if this channel is opened, the neighboring commanderies will all benefit.
translations.idiomatic: All four commanderies share this affliction—not Wuxing alone; if this channel opens, neighboring commanderies will all benefit.

sentences.zh: 不有暫勞，無由永晏。

translations.literal: Without temporary labor there can be no lasting peace.
translations.idiomatic: Without temporary labor there can be no lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 然興創事大，圖始當難。

translations.literal: Yet founding a great undertaking is difficult at the start.
translations.idiomatic: Yet founding a great undertaking is difficult at the start.

sentences.zh: 今欲且開小漕，觀試流勢，輒差烏程、武康、東遷三縣近民，即時營作。

translations.literal: Now I wish first to open a small canal and observe the flow, dispatching the nearby people of the three counties of Wucheng, Wukang, and Dongqian to work at once.
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish first to open a small canal and observe the flow, dispatching people from Wucheng, Wukang, and Dongqian to work at once.

sentences.zh: 若宜更增廣，尋更列言。

translations.literal: If it should be further enlarged, I will memorialize again in due course.
translations.idiomatic: If it should be enlarged, I will memorialize again.

sentences.zh: 昔鄭國敵將，史起畢忠，一開其說，萬世為利。

translations.literal: Formerly when Zheng was the enemy state, Shi Qi completed his loyal service—once his proposal was adopted, ten thousand generations benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when Zheng was the enemy state, Shi Qi completed loyal service—once adopted, his proposal benefited ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 嶠之所建，雖側芻蕘，如或非妄，庶幾可立。」

translations.literal: What Qiao proposes, though humble counsel, if it is not folly may perhaps be established."
translations.idiomatic: What Qiao proposes, though humble counsel, may perhaps be established."

sentences.zh: 從之；

translations.literal: This was approved;
translations.idiomatic: This was approved;

sentences.zh: 功竟不立。

translations.literal: The work was ultimately not completed.
translations.idiomatic: The work was ultimately not completed.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was granted one set of martial drums and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was granted a set of martial drums and pipes.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，出為使持節、都督南徐兗二州諸軍事、征北將軍、開府儀同三司、南徐兗二州刺史，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs of the two provinces of southern Xu and Yan, General Who Campaigns North, with office equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of the two provinces of southern Xu and Yan, his Regular Attendant status unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he went out as Bearer of the Staff, commander of southern Xu and Yan, General Who Campaigns North, with Three Excellencies honors, and inspector of southern Xu and Yan, retaining his Regular Attendant status.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遣浚率眾城瓜步山，解南兗州。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was sent to lead troops to fortify Guabu Mountain and was relieved of southern Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he led troops to fortify Guabu Mountain and was relieved of southern Yan province.

sentences.zh: 三十年，徙都督荊雍益梁甯南北秦七州諸軍事、衛將軍、開府儀同三司、荊州刺史、領護南蠻校尉，持節、常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was transferred as Commander over military affairs of the seven provinces of Jing, Yong, Yi, Liang, Ning, northern and southern Qin, Guard General, with office equal to the Three Excellencies, Inspector of Jingzhou, and concurrently Protector of the Southern Barbarians Commandant, holding the Staff and Regular Attendant status unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was transferred as commander of seven provinces including Jing and Yong, Guard General with Three Excellencies honors, inspector of Jingzhou, and Protector of the Southern Barbarians, retaining the Staff and Regular Attendant status.

sentences.zh: 浚少好文籍，姿質端妍。

translations.literal: Jun from youth loved literary works; his bearing and appearance were elegant and handsome.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jun loved literature; he was elegant and handsome in bearing.

sentences.zh: 母潘淑妃有盛寵，時六宮無主，潘專總內政。

translations.literal: His mother, Consort Pan the Cultivated, enjoyed great favor; at the time the six palaces had no chief mistress, and Pan monopolized internal administration.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Consort Pan the Cultivated, enjoyed great favor; with no empress in the six palaces, Pan monopolized internal administration.

sentences.zh: 浚人才既美，母又至愛，太祖甚留心。

translations.literal: Jun's talent was already fine, and his mother was deeply loved—the Grand Ancestor paid him great attention.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was talented and his mother deeply beloved—the Grand Ancestor paid him great attention.

sentences.zh: 建平王宏、侍中王僧綽、中書侍郎蔡興宗並以文義往復。

translations.literal: Prince of Jianping Hong, Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Sengchuo, and Secretariat Attendant-Cadet Cai Xingzong all exchanged literary correspondence with him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, Prince of Jianping, Wang Sengchuo, and Cai Xingzong all exchanged literary correspondence with him.

sentences.zh: 初，元皇后性忌，以潘氏見幸，遂以恚恨致崩，故劭深疾潘氏及浚。

translations.literal: Earlier, the primary empress was jealous by nature; because Lady Pan was favored, she died of resentment and grief, and therefore Shao deeply hated Lady Pan and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: The primary empress had been jealous; because Lady Pan was favored, she died of grief and resentment, and Shao therefore deeply hated Pan and Jun.

sentences.zh: 浚慮將來受禍，乃曲意事劭，劭與之遂善。

translations.literal: Jun, fearing future harm, therefore curried favor with Shao, and Shao became close with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing future harm, Jun curried favor with Shao until they became close.

sentences.zh: 多有過失，屢為上所詰讓，憂懼，乃與劭共為巫蠱。

translations.literal: He had many faults and was repeatedly interrogated and rebuked by the emperor; in anxiety and fear he joined Shao in witchcraft sorcery.
translations.idiomatic: He had many faults and was repeatedly rebuked by the emperor; in fear he joined Shao in witchcraft sorcery.

sentences.zh: 及出鎮京口，聽將揚州文武二千人自隨，優遊外籓，甚為得意。

translations.literal: When he went out to garrison Jingkou he was permitted to take two thousand civil and military officers of Yangzhou with him; roaming freely in an outer fief, he was greatly pleased with himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to garrison Jingkou he was allowed two thousand Yangzhou officers to accompany him; roaming in an outer fief, he was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 在外經年，又失南兗，於是複願還朝。

translations.literal: After years abroad he again lost southern Yan, and therefore wished to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: After years abroad he lost southern Yan as well and wished to return to court.

sentences.zh: 廬陵王紹以疾患解揚州，時江夏王義恭外鎮，浚謂州任自然歸己，而上以授南譙王義宣，意甚不悅。

translations.literal: Prince of Luling Shao, owing to illness, was relieved of Yangzhou; at the time Prince of Jiangxia Yigong was garrisoning abroad. Jun thought the provincial post would naturally fall to him, but the emperor gave it to Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan—he was deeply displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Luling Shao was relieved of Yangzhou due to illness while Yigong garrisoned abroad. Jun expected the post would fall to him, but the emperor gave it to Yixuan, Prince of Nanqiao—he was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 乃因員外散騎侍郎徐爰求鎮江陵，又求助於尚書僕射徐湛之。

translations.literal: He therefore, through Extraordinary Attendant-Cadet of Scattered Cavalry Xu Ai, sought to garrison Jiangling, and also sought help from Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Xu Zhanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Through Xu Ai, Extraordinary Attendant-Cadet, he sought to garrison Jiangling and also sought help from Xu Zhanzhi, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 而尚書令何尚之等咸謂浚太子次弟，不宜遠出。

translations.literal: But Director of the Masters of Writing He Shangzhi and others all held that Jun, as the crown prince's younger brother, should not be sent far away.
translations.idiomatic: But He Shangzhi, Director of the Masters of Writing, and others held that Jun, as the crown prince's younger brother, should not be sent far away.

sentences.zh: 上以上流之重，宜有至親，故以授浚。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the weight of the upper Yangzi required a close kin, therefore gave it to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because the upper Yangzi required a close kinsman, gave the post to Jun.

sentences.zh: 時浚入朝，遣還京，為行留處分。

translations.literal: At that time Jun was entering court; he was sent back to the capital for arrangements regarding his departure and stay.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was then entering court and was sent back to the capital for departure arrangements.

sentences.zh: 至京數日而巫蠱事發，時二十九年七月也。

translations.literal: Within several days at the capital the witchcraft affair broke out—it was the seventh month of the twenty-ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: Within days at the capital the witchcraft affair broke out—the seventh month of the twenty-ninth year.

sentences.zh: 上惋歎彌日，謂潘淑妃曰：「太子圖富貴，更是一理。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in grief for days and said to Consort Pan the Cultivated, "The crown prince seeking wealth and rank is one thing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved for days and said to Consort Pan, "The crown prince seeking power is one thing.

sentences.zh: 虎頭複如北，非複思慮所及。

translations.literal: Tiger Head acting again like this is no longer within what one could have foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger Head acting thus is beyond what one could have foreseen.

sentences.zh: 汝母子豈可一日無我耶！」

translations.literal: How can you mother and son go a single day without me!"
translations.idiomatic: How can you mother and son endure a single day without me!"

sentences.zh: 浚小名虎頭。

translations.literal: Jun's childhood name was Tiger Head.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's childhood name was Tiger Head.

sentences.zh: 使左右硃法瑜密責讓浚，辭甚哀切，並賜書曰：「鸚鵡事想汝已聞，汝亦何至迷惑乃爾。

translations.literal: He had his attendant Zhu Fayu secretly rebuke and question Jun in words very mournful and urgent, and also sent a letter saying, "You must have heard of the Yingwu affair—how could you become so deluded?
translations.idiomatic: He had Zhu Fayu secretly rebuke Jun in urgent, mournful words and sent a letter: "You must have heard of the Yingwu affair—how could you become so deluded?

sentences.zh: 且沈懷遠何人，其詎能為汝隱此耶？

translations.literal: Besides, what sort of man is Shen Huaiyuan that he could hide this for you?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, what sort of man is Shen Huaiyuan that he could hide this for you?

sentences.zh: 故使法瑜口宣，投筆惋慨。」

translations.literal: Therefore I have Fayu announce this orally; I set down the brush in grief and indignation."
translations.idiomatic: I have Fayu announce this orally; I set down the brush in grief."

sentences.zh: 浚慚懼，不知所答。

translations.literal: Jun was ashamed and afraid, not knowing how to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was ashamed and afraid, not knowing how to answer.

sentences.zh: 浚還京，本暫去，上怒，不聽歸。

translations.literal: Jun had returned to the capital intending only a brief absence, but the emperor in anger would not permit his return.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had meant only a brief stay in the capital, but the angry emperor would not let him return.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，中書侍郎蔡興宗問建平王宏曰：「歲無複幾，征北何當至？」

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year Secretariat Attendant-Cadet Cai Xingzong asked Prince of Jianping Hong, "The year has little left—when will the Northern Campaigning General arrive?"
translations.idiomatic: That twelfth month Cai Xingzong asked Hong, Prince of Jianping, "The year has little left—when will the Northern Campaigning General arrive?"

sentences.zh: 宏歎息良久曰：「年內何必還。」

translations.literal: Hong sighed for a long while and said, "Within the year he need not return."
translations.idiomatic: Hong sighed and said, "He need not return within the year."

sentences.zh: 在京以沈懷遠為長流參軍，每夕輒開便門為微行。

translations.literal: In the capital he made Shen Huaiyuan his chief roaming staff officer; every evening he would open the side gate for secret outings.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he made Shen Huaiyuan chief roaming staff officer and each evening opened the side gate for secret outings.

sentences.zh: 上聞，殺其嬖人楊承先。

translations.literal: When the emperor learned of this, he killed Jun's favorite Yang Chengxian.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, he killed Jun's favorite Yang Chengxian.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，荊州事方行，二月，浚還朝。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year the Jingzhou appointment was about to proceed; in the second month Jun returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month the Jingzhou appointment was to proceed; in the second month Jun returned to court.

sentences.zh: 十四日，臨軒受拜。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day he received investiture facing the hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth he received investiture facing the hall.

sentences.zh: 其日，藏嚴道育事發，明旦浚入謝，上容色非常。

translations.literal: That day the matter of hiding Yan Daoyu broke out; the next morning when Jun entered to pay respects, the emperor's expression was extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: That day the matter of hiding Yan Daoyu broke out; the next morning when Jun paid respects, the emperor's expression was extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 其夕，即加詰問，浚唯謝罪而已。

translations.literal: That evening he was immediately interrogated; Jun could only beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: That evening he was interrogated; Jun could only beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 潘淑妃抱持浚，泣涕謂曰：「汝始咒詛事發，猶冀刻己思愆，何意忽藏嚴道育耶？

translations.literal: Consort Pan the Cultivated embraced Jun, weeping and saying, "When the cursing affair first broke out, I still hoped you would restrain yourself and reflect—who imagined you would still hide Yan Daoyu?
translations.idiomatic: Consort Pan embraced Jun, weeping: "When the cursing affair broke out I hoped you would reform—who imagined you would still hide Yan Daoyu?

sentences.zh: 上責汝深，至我叩頭乞恩，意永不釋。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked you severely; I knocked my head begging grace, yet his mind will never release this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked you severely; I begged for grace, yet his anger will never release.

sentences.zh: 今日用活何為，可送藥來，當先自取盡，不忍見汝禍敗。」

translations.literal: What is the use of living now? Send poison—I will take it first myself; I cannot bear to see you ruined in disaster."
translations.idiomatic: What is the use of living? Send poison—I will take it first; I cannot bear to see you ruined."

sentences.zh: 浚奮衣而去，曰：「天下事尋自當判，願小寬憂煎，必不上累。」

translations.literal: Jun flung aside his robes and left, saying, "The realm's affairs will soon be decided; please ease your grief a little—you will surely not be implicated."
translations.idiomatic: Jun flung aside his robes and left: "The realm's affairs will soon be decided; ease your grief—you will not be implicated."

sentences.zh: 劭入弑之旦，浚在西州，府舍人硃法瑜奔告浚曰：「台內叫喚，宮門皆閉，道上傳太子反，未測禍變所至。」

translations.literal: On the morning Shao entered to commit regicide, Jun was at the Western Quarter; his household attendant Zhu Fayu ran to tell Jun, "Inside the palace there is shouting; the palace gates are all closed; on the roads they say the crown prince has rebelled—I cannot tell where disaster has reached."
translations.idiomatic: On the morning of the regicide Jun was at the Western Quarter; Zhu Fayu ran to tell him, "The palace is shouting, the gates are closed, and the roads say the crown prince has rebelled—disaster has struck."

sentences.zh: 浚陽驚曰：「今當奈何？」

translations.literal: Jun pretended surprise and said, "What should we do now?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun feigned surprise: "What should we do now?"

sentences.zh: 法瑜勸入據石頭。

translations.literal: Fayu urged him to enter and hold Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Fayu urged him to seize Shitou.

sentences.zh: 浚未得劭信，不知事之濟不，騷擾未知所為。

translations.literal: Jun had not yet received Shao's message and did not know whether the affair would succeed; agitated, he did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Without word from Shao Jun did not know whether the coup would succeed and was agitated, not knowing what to do.

sentences.zh: 將軍王慶曰：「今宮內有變，未知主上安危，預在臣子。

translations.literal: General Wang Qing said, "Now there is turmoil within the palace and we do not know whether the lord above is safe—this is the moment for subjects.
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Qing said, "There is turmoil in the palace and we do not know whether the emperor is safe—this is the moment for subjects.

sentences.zh: 當投袂赴難。

translations.literal: We should throw aside our sleeves and rush to the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: We should throw aside our sleeves and rush to help.

sentences.zh: 憑城自守，非臣節也。」

translations.literal: Holding the city and defending ourselves is not the conduct of a minister."
translations.idiomatic: Holding the city in defense is not the conduct of a minister."

sentences.zh: 浚不聽，乃從南門出，徑向石頭，文武從者千餘人。

translations.literal: Jun would not listen and instead went out through the Southern Gate, heading straight for Shitou, with more than a thousand civil and military followers.
translations.idiomatic: Jun would not listen and went out the Southern Gate straight for Shitou with more than a thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 時南平王鑠守石頭，兵士亦千余人。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Nanping Shuo was guarding Shitou with likewise more than a thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo, Prince of Nanping, was then guarding Shitou with more than a thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 俄而劭遣張超之馳馬召浚，浚屏人問狀，即戎服乘馬而去。

translations.literal: Soon Shao sent Zhang Chaozhi galloping to summon Jun; Jun dismissed those present, asked the situation, then donned armor, mounted, and went.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shao sent Zhang Chaozhi to summon Jun; Jun dismissed those present, learned the situation, donned armor, mounted, and went.

sentences.zh: 硃法瑜固止浚，浚不從。

translations.literal: Zhu Fayu firmly tried to stop Jun, but Jun would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fayu tried to stop him, but Jun would not listen.

sentences.zh: 出至中門，王慶又諫曰：「太子反逆，天下怨憤。

translations.literal: When he reached the middle gate Wang Qing again remonstrated, "The crown prince has rebelled; all under Heaven resent him.
translations.idiomatic: At the middle gate Wang Qing remonstrated again, "The crown prince has rebelled; the realm resents him.

sentences.zh: 明公但當堅閉城門，坐食積粟，不過三日，凶黨自離。

translations.literal: Your Lordship need only firmly close the city gates and live on stored grain—within three days the villainous party will scatter of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Close the gates and live on stored grain—within three days the rebels will scatter.

sentences.zh: 公情事如此，今豈宜去。」

translations.literal: Your situation being as it is, how can you now go?"
translations.idiomatic: In your situation, how can you go now?"

sentences.zh: 浚曰：「皇太子令，敢有複言者斬！」

translations.literal: Jun said, "The crown prince has ordered it—whoever speaks again shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "The crown prince orders it—whoever speaks again shall be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 既入，見劭，勸殺荀赤松等。

translations.literal: Once inside he saw Shao and urged the killing of Xun Chisong and others.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside he saw Shao and urged killing Xun Chisong and others.

sentences.zh: 劭謂浚曰：「潘淑妃遂為亂兵所害。」

translations.literal: Shao told Jun, "Consort Pan the Cultivated was killed by the mutinous soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: Shao told Jun, "Consort Pan was killed by mutinous soldiers."

sentences.zh: 浚曰：「此是下情由來所願。」

translations.literal: Jun said, "That has long been my wish from below."
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "That has long been my dearest wish."

sentences.zh: 其悖逆乃如此。

translations.literal: His perversity was to such a degree.
translations.idiomatic: His perversity was to such a degree.

sentences.zh: 及劭將敗，勸劭入海，輦珍寶繒帛下船，與劭書曰：「船故未至，今晚期當於此下物令畢，願速敕謝賜出船艦。

translations.literal: When Shao was about to be defeated, Jun urged him to flee to sea, loading precious treasures and silks onto boats, and wrote to Shao, "The boats have not yet arrived; tonight I expect to finish loading goods here—please quickly order the grant of ships.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao was about to fall, Jun urged flight by sea, loading treasures onto boats, and wrote, "The boats have not arrived; tonight I expect to finish loading—please order ships sent quickly.

sentences.zh: 尼已入台，願與之明日決也。

translations.literal: The nun has already entered the palace—I wish to settle with her tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The nun has entered the palace—I wish to settle matters with her tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 臣猶謂車駕應出此，不爾無以鎮物情。」

translations.literal: I still think the imperial carriage should come out here; otherwise there is no way to steady popular sentiment."
translations.idiomatic: I still think the imperial carriage should come here; otherwise popular sentiment cannot be steadied."

sentences.zh: 人情離散，故行計不果。

translations.literal: Popular sentiment scattered, and therefore the plan was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Popular sentiment scattered, and the plan failed.

sentences.zh: 浚書所雲尼，即嚴道育也。

translations.literal: The "nun" Jun's letter mentions is Yan Daoyu.
translations.idiomatic: The "nun" in Jun's letter is Yan Daoyu.

sentences.zh: 及劭入井，高禽于井中牽出之。

translations.literal: When Shao entered the well, Gao Qin pulled him out from within it.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao hid in the well, Gao Qin pulled him out.

sentences.zh: 劭問禽曰：「天子何在？」

translations.literal: Shao asked Qin, "Where is the Son of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao asked Qin, "Where is the Son of Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 禽曰：「至尊近在新亭。」

translations.literal: Qin said, "His Majesty is recently at Xinting."
translations.idiomatic: Qin said, "His Majesty is at Xinting."

sentences.zh: 將劭至殿前，臧質見之慟哭，劭曰：「天地所不覆載，丈人何為見哭。」

translations.literal: They brought Shao before the hall; when Zang Zhi saw him he wailed; Shao said, "What heaven and earth do not cover and bear—why does Elder Sir weep for me?"
translations.idiomatic: They brought Shao before the hall; Zang Zhi wailed; Shao said, "What heaven and earth do not cover—why weep for me?"

sentences.zh: 質因辨其逆狀，答曰：「先朝當見枉廢，不能作獄中囚，問計于蕭斌，斌見勸如此。」

translations.literal: Zhi therefore laid out his rebellious conduct; Shao replied, "The former court was wrongly going to depose me—I could not be a prisoner in the cells and asked counsel of Xiao Bin; Bin encouraged me thus."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi laid out his crimes; Shao replied, "The court was going to depose me—I could not be a prisoner and asked Xiao Bin, who encouraged this."

sentences.zh: 又語質曰：「可得為啟，乞遠徙不？」

translations.literal: He also said to Zhi, "Can you memorialize for me, begging exile far away?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked Zhi, "Can you memorialize begging exile for me?"

sentences.zh: 質答曰：「主上近在航南，自當有處分。」

translations.literal: Zhi replied, "The lord above is recently south of the crossing—he will naturally have a disposition."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi replied, "The emperor is south of the crossing—he will decide."

sentences.zh: 縛劭於馬上，防送軍門。

translations.literal: They bound Shao on his horse and escorted him under guard to the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: They bound Shao on his horse and escorted him to the army gate.

sentences.zh: 既至牙下，據鞍顧望，太尉江夏王義恭與諸王皆共臨視之。

translations.literal: When he reached the headquarters he sat in the saddle looking about; Grand Commandant Prince of Jiangxia Yigong and the princes all viewed him together.
translations.idiomatic: At headquarters he looked about from the saddle; Yigong and the princes all viewed him.

sentences.zh: 義恭詰劭曰：「我背逆歸順，有何大罪，頓殺我家十二兒？」

translations.literal: Yigong interrogated Shao, "I turned from rebellion to loyalty—what great crime had I, that you suddenly killed twelve sons of my house?"
translations.idiomatic: Yigong demanded, "I turned to loyalty—what crime warranted killing twelve of my sons?"

sentences.zh: 劭答曰：「殺諸弟，此事負阿父。」

translations.literal: Shao replied, "Killing your younger brothers—that matter wronged Uncle."
translations.idiomatic: Shao replied, "Killing your brothers—that wronged you, Uncle."

sentences.zh: 江湛妻庾氏乘車罵之，龐秀之亦加誚讓，劭厲聲曰：「汝輩複何煩爾！」

translations.literal: Jiang Zhan's wife, the Lady Yu, came in a carriage to revile him; Pang Xiuzhi also added reproach; Shao shouted, "Why do you people trouble yourselves over this!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhan's wife Yu reviled him from her carriage; Pang Xiuzhi reproached him; Shao shouted, "Why trouble yourselves!"

sentences.zh: 先殺其四子，謂南平王鑠曰：「此何有哉。」

translations.literal: First they killed his four sons, Shao saying to Prince of Nanping Shuo, "What is there to this?"
translations.idiomatic: First they killed his four sons; Shao told Shuo, Prince of Nanping, "What is there to this?"

sentences.zh: 乃斬劭於牙下。

translations.literal: Then they beheaded Shao below the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Then they beheaded Shao below the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 臨刑歎曰：「不圖宗室一至於此。」

translations.literal: Facing execution he sighed, "I never imagined the imperial clan would come to this."
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution he sighed, "I never imagined the imperial clan would come to this."

sentences.zh: 劭、浚及劭四子偉之、迪之、彬之、其一未有名；

translations.literal: Shao, Jun, and Shao's four sons Weizhi, Dizhi, Binzhi, and one not yet named;
translations.idiomatic: Shao, Jun, and Shao's four sons Weizhi, Dizhi, Binzhi, and one not yet named;

sentences.zh: 浚三子長文、長仁、長道，並梟首大航，暴屍於市。

translations.literal: Jun's three sons Changwen, Changren, and Changdao were all displayed at the Great Crossing with heads hung, their corpses exposed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's three sons Changwen, Changren, and Changdao were beheaded at the Great Crossing and their corpses exposed in the market.

sentences.zh: 劭妻殷氏賜死于廷尉，臨死，謂獄丞江恪曰：「汝家骨肉相殘害，何以枉殺天下無罪人。」

translations.literal: Shao's wife, the Lady Yin, was granted death in the Ministry of Justice; facing death she told prison aide Jiang Ke, "Your house butchers its own flesh—why wrongly kill innocent people under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao's wife Lady Yin was executed in the Ministry of Justice; facing death she told prison aide Jiang Ke, "Your house butchers its own—why kill innocents?"

sentences.zh: 恪曰：「受拜皇后，非罪而何？」

translations.literal: Ke said, "You received investiture as empress—if not a crime, what is?"
translations.idiomatic: Ke said, "You accepted the empress title—if not a crime, what is?"

sentences.zh: 殷氏曰：「此權時爾，當以鸚鵡為後也。」

translations.literal: The Lady Yin said, "That was only expedient—I would have made Yingwu successor."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yin said, "That was expedient—I would have made Yingwu empress."

sentences.zh: 浚妻褚氏，丹陽尹湛之女，湛之南奔之始，即見離絕，故免於誅。

translations.literal: Jun's wife, the Lady Chu, was the daughter of Intendant of Danyang Chu Chenzhi; when Chenzhi first fled south they were already separated, and therefore she escaped execution.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's wife Lady Chu was daughter of Chu Chenzhi; when he fled south they were already separated, so she escaped execution.

sentences.zh: 其餘子女妾媵，並於獄賜死。

translations.literal: The remaining sons, daughters, concubines, and attendants were all granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Their remaining children, concubines, and attendants were all executed in prison.

sentences.zh: 投劭、浚屍首于江，其餘同逆，及王羅漢等，皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Shao and Jun's corpses were thrown into the river; the rest of the fellow rebels and Wang Luohan and others were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Shao and Jun's corpses were thrown into the river; fellow rebels including Wang Luohan were all executed.

sentences.zh: 張超之聞兵入，遂走至合殿故基，正於禦床之所，為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: When Zhang Chaozhi heard the army had entered, he fled to the old foundation of the Unified Hall, right at the place of the imperial couch, and was killed by the mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chaozhi heard the army had entered, he fled to the old site of the Unified Hall at the imperial couch and was killed.

sentences.zh: 割腸刳心，臠剖其肉，諸將生啖之，焚其頭骨。

translations.literal: They cut open his belly and heart, sliced his flesh, and the generals ate it raw; his skull was burned.
translations.idiomatic: They cut open his belly and heart, sliced his flesh; generals ate it raw and burned his skull.

sentences.zh: 當時不見傳國璽，問劭，雲：「在嚴道育處。」

translations.literal: At the time the imperial seal of transmission was not seen; Shao was asked and said, "It is with Yan Daoyu."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial seal of transmission was missing; asked, Shao said, "It is with Yan Daoyu."

sentences.zh: 就取得之。

translations.literal: They went and obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: They went and obtained it.

sentences.zh: 道育、鸚鵡並都街鞭殺，於石頭四望山下焚其屍，揚灰于江。

translations.literal: Daoyu and Yingwu were both flogged to death in the street; at Shitou's Four-View Mountain their corpses were burned and the ash scattered on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu and Yingwu were flogged to death in the street; at Four-View Mountain below Shitou their corpses were burned and the ash scattered on the river.

sentences.zh: 毀劭東宮所住齋，汙瀦其處。

translations.literal: Shao's Eastern Palace fasting chambers were destroyed and the site defiled with dung.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's Eastern Palace fasting chambers were destroyed and the site defiled.

sentences.zh: 封高禽新陽縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Gao Qin was enfeoffed as Baron of Xinyang with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qin was enfeoffed as Baron of Xinyang with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 追贈潘淑妃長寧園夫人，置守塚。

translations.literal: Consort Pan the Cultivated was posthumously honored as Lady of the Everlasting Peace Garden, with tomb guardians appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Pan was posthumously honored as Lady of the Everlasting Peace Garden, with tomb guardians appointed.

sentences.zh: 偽司隸校尉殷沖，丹陽尹尹弘，並賜死。

translations.literal: The false Director of Retainers Yin Chong and Intendant of Danyang Yin Hong were both granted death.
translations.idiomatic: The false Director of Retainers Yin Chong and intendant Yin Hong were both executed.

sentences.zh: 沖為劭草立符文，又妃叔父也。

translations.literal: Chong drafted the ritual texts for Shao and was also the empress's uncle by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Chong drafted Shao's ritual texts and was also the empress's uncle by marriage.

sentences.zh: 弘二月二十一日平旦入直，至西掖門，聞宮中有變，率城內禦兵至閣道下。

translations.literal: Hong entered duty at dawn on the twenty-first day of the second month, reaching the Western Corner Gate; hearing turmoil in the palace, he led the capital's palace guards to below the covered passage.
translations.idiomatic: Hong entered duty at dawn on the twenty-first of the second month; hearing palace turmoil, he led capital guards to the covered passage.

sentences.zh: 及聞劭入，惶怖通啟，求受處分，又為劭簡配兵士，盡其心力。

translations.literal: When he heard Shao had entered, he in terror reported and begged to be dealt with; he also selected and assigned soldiers for Shao, exhausting his utmost effort.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Shao had entered, he reported in terror and begged judgment; he also selected soldiers for Shao with all his effort.

sentences.zh: 弘，天水冀人，司州刺史沖弟也。

translations.literal: Hong was a native of Ji in Tianshui and the younger brother of Inspector of Sizhou Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was from Ji in Tianshui and the younger brother of Chong, inspector of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 為太祖所委任。

translations.literal: He was entrusted by the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor entrusted him with important duties.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，曆太子左右衛率、左右衛將軍，囗人官爵高下，皆以委之。

translations.literal: During Yuanjia he served successively as Left and Right Guard Commander of the crown prince and as Left and Right Guard General; the rank and titles of inner personnel were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanjia he served as Left and Right Guard Commander and Left and Right Guard General for the crown prince; rank and titles for inner personnel were all entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：甚矣哉，宋氏之家難也。

translations.literal: The historian says: How extreme indeed is the Liu Song family's calamity!
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: How extreme indeed is the house of Song's family calamity!

sentences.zh: 自赫胥以降，立號皇王，統天南面，未聞斯禍。

translations.literal: From Hexu downward, when titles of emperor and king were established and rulers faced south to govern all under Heaven, such a calamity has not been heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Since the age of Hexu, when rulers took the titles of emperor and king and faced south to govern the realm, no such calamity has been heard of.

sentences.zh: 唯荊、莒二國，棄夏即戎，武靈胡服，亦背華典，戕賊之釁，事起肌膚，而因心之重，獨止此代。

translations.literal: Only the states of Jing and Ju abandoned Xia for the Rong, and King Wuling's barbarian dress also turned from Hua norms—the omen of slaughter arose from the flesh, yet the weight of inner motive was confined to those ages alone.
translations.idiomatic: Only Jing and Ju abandoned civilization for barbarism, and King Wuling's foreign dress also departed from Chinese norms—slaughter began in the flesh, yet the weight of motive was confined to those ages alone.

sentences.zh: 難興天屬，穢流床笫，愛敬之道，頓滅一時，生民得無左衽，亦為幸矣！

translations.literal: Calamity rising among heaven's kin, filth flowing upon the bed and mat—the way of love and respect was extinguished in a moment; that the people were not turned to left-side dress may also count as fortune!
translations.idiomatic: Calamity rising among the emperor's own kin, filth staining the bedchamber—the way of love and respect was extinguished in a moment; that the people were not turned to barbarian ways may itself count as fortune!
